articles.title: NHL Frozen Frenzy 2026 Live Blog: Red Wings, Canadiens, Maple Leafs, Jets And Oilers Headline Nonstop Action
articles.summary: Thirty-two teams collide in a sixteen-game marathon featuring Ovechkin’s farewell in Carolina, Bedard’s anticipated return, and a high-stakes goalie controve...
articles.body:
Thirty-two teams. Sixteen games. All in one night.

Yes, it's NHL Frozen Frenzy — and this year's eight hours or so of madness promises not to disappoint.

Connor Bedard is (reportedly) back with the Chicago Blackhawks. Alex Ovechkin is back — for the last time? — in Carolina. And Mikko Rantanen is back playing against his former team, the Colorado Avalanche.

Will Dylan Larkin get booed by the home fans in Detroit? Will Brady Tkachuk finally score his first goal as a Florida Panther?" Will the Toronto Maple Leafs escape their road trip out west with five out of a possible six points?

More importantly, will we report on all the action? Yes!

Don't forget to follow us @thehockeynews.com and drop a comment or question below in the comments.

"Told it's really quiet. No momentum for a trade right now. That said I get the sense the relationship between larkin and the red wings is at such a place it's just a matter of when not if." — ESPN's Emily Kaplan on Dylan Larkin

1-0 for Devils on a goal from Evan Rodrigues, his first since being traded to New Jersey.

Devils outshooting Red Wings 16-3 after 20 minutes. The score is tied 1-1.

Does Connor Hellebuyck want to play in New Jersey? The Red Wings have given up two goals on four shots.

Jack Hughes scores the overtime winner for New Jersey, ending a wild back-and-forth battle to kick off the Frozen Frenzy.

A bit of good news for the Red Wings, who appear to have signed Alex DeBrincat to a seven-year extension with a $13-million cap hit. The contract, which kicks in next season, makes him the 13th highest-paid NHLer — for now.

Columbus scores and Matthew Knies picks up the assist. The ex-Leaf now has five points in five games.

Brady Tkachuk scores his first goals since joining the Panthers. And, of course, Matthew gets the assist.

Matthew finds Brady alone in the slot for his second.

Four points each for the Tkachuk brothers, who pick up assists on a goal from Carter Verhaeghe.

Kids, don't try this at home: Mathieu Olivier gets a five-minute major and a game misconduct for spearing Uvis (in his) Balinskis. Ouch!

Another assist for Matthew Tkachuk. Watch out, Connor McDavid (10 assists), but Tkachuk is now up to seven assists in seven games.

Big night from the players who were off to cold starts, as Sam Reinhart scores his second of the game.

Is a goalie controversy brewing in Montreal? The Habs appear to be starting Jacob Fowler for the third game in a row.

Buffalo scores on a goal from Owen Zellweger, just first since joining the Sabres I a trade for Bowen Byram.

Tough to watch as linesman falls awkwardly on his ankle . Being helped off the ice.

Lane Hutson gets his first on a point shot on the PP. It was a wrister. But it was a snipe .

Save of the Year alert : UPL stops the Habs on a two-on-none.

Noah Dobson takes a shot off the jaw. With Michael Matheson also out, this is not good for the Habs' defense.

What's going on with Montreal in the third period? Buffalo scores twice in under six minutes to tie things up 3-3, despite being outshot 23-14.

For the second straight game, the Habs are heading to overtime.

Carolina was where Alex Ovechkin was drafted No. 1 overall in 2004 . Twenty-two years later, he's playing in his final regular season game in Raleigh, N.C.

According to @ryanhenkel_ , the Canes recognized Ovechkin during a stoppage in play and he received a standing ovation .

Carolina loses Taylor Hall, who "was ruled out in the second period of Tuesday's game against the Washington Capitals due to an upper-body injury." Hall took a hard hit from Justin Sourdif late in the first period.

Looks like Porter Martone and Matvei Michkov will play together on a line.

Bobby McMann scores his third of the season. With 29 goals split between Toronto and Seattle, he was technically the Kraken's leading goal scorer last season.

Make that seven goals in eight game for breakout candidate Lafreniere.

According to reporter Steve Warne , the Senators have three defensemen tonight who each have played in 10 NHL games or less.

It appears that Zee's Buium has been dropped to the Canucks' third defense pairing alongside Luke Schenn.

Calder Trophy Watch: Chicago's Anton Frondell picks up his fifth assist of the season. He now has five points in seven games.

Sidney Crosby scores his first of the season. Last year, he finished with 29.

From @OHaraSports : "Mackenzie Blackwood is 0-4-1 in six regular season games against the Dallas Stars. He holds a 4.10 goals against average and a .887 save percentage in those appearances. Two of those games came when he was was with the New Jersey Devils, three with the San Jose Sharks, and one with the Colorado Avalanche."

articles.title: Red Bull sends warning to F1 rivals with engine development admission
articles.summary: Red Bull technical director Pierre Wache has rated the team's first in-house Formula 1 power unit project just four or five out of 10
articles.body:
Ask most engineers to grade their own work at four or five out of 10 and you'd brace for bad news. Pierre Wache, Red Bull Racing's technical director, offered that score for the team's first homemade Formula 1 power unit, and it feels like a threat to the rest of the grid. Put simply, Red Bull thinks its in-house engine is somewhere between 40 and 50% of the way to where it can be, and it considers that a good place to start.

Asked by RacingNews365 to rate the project on a scale of one to 10, Wache said: "I'd say a four or a five." When the follow-up asked whether that leaves a lot of room to grow, he warned: "Absolutely, the potential is massive."

Throughout its two decades in Formula 1 from 2005 to 2025, Red Bull relied on external engine manufacturers - Cosworth, Ferrari , Renault, and Honda among them - rather than developing powerplants in-house. Beginning this season, this has changed as the team undertakes its first independent engine program in partnership with Ford. The unit is the 1.6-litre turbocharged V6 known as the Red Bull Ford DM01, built by Red Bull Powertrains in Milton Keynes, where Ben Hodgkinson leads the engine side while Wache handles the RB22 chassis.

According to RacingNews365 , the FIA's ADUO assessment revealed that Red Bull's internal combustion engine generated the highest output among all competitors on the grid. That makes a self-assessment of four or five rather intriguing. If this is the half-finished version, other teams likely have a reason to be nervous.

"You have to do more, and you also feel more responsible for what we can achieve," he said. He also sees the upside of owning the whole package: "Ultimately, we'll have more freedom. As you say, it's a success story. But you know, the journey isn't over yet. We have plenty of stuff to improve together."

Does the in-house building make life easier?

"So, I wouldn't say it's easier, because we have a lot more capacity and a lot more possibilities that we haven't explored and exploited yet.

"But the capacity and the potential to have a better performance are higher, and this is why we are doing this."

Engine people and chassis people don't think alike

Putting an engine department and a chassis department under one roof sounds like the most organised option, but Wache admits it wasn't as easy as it sounds. "The collaboration and the integration within the team are taking time because the way we work is a little bit different," he said, before adding: "Just by nature, the people on the engine and chassis side are quite different."

A big reason is the calendar. An engine takes far longer to develop than a chassis, so the two groups see problems and deadlines differently. "Anyway, it's a learning process for the full team because the lead time on a chassis is a lot quicker than an engine, so the way you see stuff is different, and the way we work with them is different compared to what we used to do when we were a customer."

Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

As a customer, Red Bull simply received a finished power unit and designed around it. Now the chassis team's tight turnarounds have to match an engine program that thinks in much longer cycles.

That is the real significance of the four-or-five rating. It suggests Red Bull is still building its own working processes as much as it is building horsepower, and that the performance it has shown so far comes before those habits have fully settled. A team admitting it is only about halfway through its first engine, while already becoming the benchmark, is either being very modest or very confident. With Red Bull, it's usually the second.

articles.title: Brandon Woodruff shares injury update as Brewers push toward World Series
articles.summary: The Milwaukee Brewers currently hold a 2-0 lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. Milwaukee is in the driver’s seat,...
articles.body:
The Milwaukee Brewers currently hold a 2-0 lead over the Los Angeles Dodgers in the National League Championship Series. Milwaukee is in the driver's seat , but there is still work to do as the best-of-seven NLCS shifts back to Dodger Stadium in LA. One pitcher who could give the Brewers a boost is Brandon Woodruff . It remains to be seen when he could return from his shoulder injury, but reports have suggested the Fall Classic remains in play for Woodruff — if Milwaukee reaches it, of course.

Woodruff threw a bullpen session and shared an injury update on Tuesday at Dodger Stadium, via Curt Hogg of the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel.

"Brandon Woodruff threw a 31-pitch bullpen this afternoon at Dodger Stadium. The intent is being ramped up, and facing batters could be next. How's the stuff? 'If you ask me, it's pretty good,'" Hogg reported on X, formerly Twitter.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Woodruff would likely return in a bullpen role. He probably won't have enough time to build up as a starter. The fact that he threw 31 pitches on Tuesday is encouraging. If he can face batters without any issues, being activated for the World Series could be a possibility.

For now, Milwaukee is focused on the series against Los Angeles. The Brewers may hold a series lead, but they know what the Dodgers are capable of. This is an LA ball club that is not going to go away quietly.

Game 3 of the NLCS between the Brewers and Dodgers in Los Angeles is scheduled for 8 PM ET.

articles.title: Ex-Commanders WR Suddenly Cut by NFL Team Before Week 6
articles.summary: The Washington Commanders have been the story of Week 5 after the way their matchup with the New York Giants concluded.Ultimately, a late-game blunder by the...
articles.body:
The Washington Commanders have been the story of Week 5 after the way their matchup with the New York Giants concluded.

Ultimately, a late-game blunder by the Commanders led to a 27-27 tie.

Now sitting at 1-3-1, Washington shifts its focus to Week 6, when it takes on the unbeaten San Francisco 49ers on "Monday Night Football."

Ahead of Week 6, the Commanders saw one of their former wide receivers hit the open market on Tuesday.

The Baltimore Ravens released 33-year-old journeyman wide receiver Chris Moore, who signed with the team on July 24.

Baltimore announced the move, writing, "We have released WR Chris Moore. We have also released WR Xavier Guillory from the Practice Squad."

Reports suggest Moore could re-sign with the Ravens ' practice squad as a vested veteran who doesn't have to clear waivers.

Moore's NFL Career and Time With Commanders

The Ravens drafted Moore in 2016, and he spent the first five years of his career in Baltimore before stints with the Houston Texans, Tennessee Titans, Arizona Cardinals and Commanders in 2024 and 2025.

Moore didn't record any stats during his first season in Washington in 2024. However, he appeared in 14 games last season and started five, hauling in 11 receptions for 207 yards and one touchdown.

He has caught three passes for 63 yards and a touchdown this season with Baltimore. Across his career, Moore has recorded 152 receptions for 1,980 yards and 10 touchdowns.

Moore could give the Commanders another depth option at wide receiver, especially since he is familiar with Daniels and head coach Dan Quinn.

Washington has also dealt with injuries at the position through the first five weeks of the season.

However, no reports have indicated that Washington is pursuing any wide receivers on the open market.

articles.title: Four Goals Not Enough for Red Wings vs. Devils
articles.summary: The Detroit Red Wings’ experiment of moving Emmitt Finnie to center seems to be paying off but it won’t matter […]
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings' experiment of moving Emmitt Finnie to center seems to be paying off but it won't matter if the team can't play an effective overall game with more consistency.

Finnie's line, which includes rookie Michael Brandsegg-Nygard and Alex DeBrincat produced four goals. However, that wasn't enough as the Devils pulled out a 5-4 overtime win on a Jack Hughes game-winner.

DeBrincat scored twice, and Finnie and Brandsegg-Ngyard scored once for the Red Wings. Each of them was plus-4. DeBrincat's second goal tied the game 4-4 early in the third period.

Andrew Copp was minus-3 in the first 40 minutes of the game.

The Red Wings went with 11 forwards and seven defensemen again in this game. Nate Danielson was the scratch up front. . . Defenseman Andreas Englund posted five hits for the Red Wings in the first two periods… Anton Johansson drew an assist on Finnie's goal for his first NHL point. . . . The Devils erased a 2-1 Detroit lead with three second period goals (by former Red Wings player Anthony Mantha, plus Nico Hischier and Jesper Bratt.)

Detroit goalie John Gibson has given up 10 goals in his past two starts for the Red Wings.

articles.title: Alex DeBrincat's 3 points not enough for Red Wings in OT loss to Devils
articles.summary: Alex DeBrincat had two goals and an assist for the Detroit Red Wings in a 5-4 overtime loss to the New Jersey Devils.
articles.body:
The second line answered for the Detroit Red Wings time and again, pushing back against an early onslaught.

Returning to Little Caesars Arena for another week, the Wings took on the New Jersey Devils in a battle of two of the top-shooting teams in the NHL. One of them backed that up from the start on on Tuesday, Oct. 13, and it wasn't the home team.

Emmitt Finnie and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, both 21 years old, set up each other's goals, and veteran Alex DeBrincat, the left wing on the line, also had a multi-point night, but the Wings had to settle for one point when Jack Hughes scored in overtime to hand the Wings a 5-4 loss, dropping them to 1-3-2 on the season.

DeBrincat celebrated his second goal and third point of the night 5:46 into the third period when he one-timed a pass by Moritz Seider, tying the game.

See Detroit Red Wings return home for matchup with New Jersey Devils

Marco Kasper, J.T. Compher and Mason Appleton remained sidelined by injuries, and Nate Danielson was scratched from the lineup as the Wings went with 11 forwards and seven defensemen for the fourth time this season. Up front, Dylan Larkin was with Viktor Arvidsson and Lucas Raymond, Emmitt Finnie with Alex DeBrincat and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard, Andrew Copp with Michael Rasmussen and Keegan Kolesar, and Sheldon Dries and Carter Mazur saw spot duty.

On the back end, Moritz Seider paired with Ben Chiarot, Justin Faulk with Albert Johansson, Anton Johansson with Andreas Englund and Axel Sandin-Pellikka also played.

The Wings couldn't get out of their zone the first several minutes and eventually it caught up to them with Stefan Noesen maneuvering a loose puck at his legs over to Evan Rodrigues for a 1-0 lead at 6:07, with shots at 3-0 at the time. Ex-Wing Anthony Mantha drew the second assist. It wasn't until the midpoint of the period that Jake Allen had to make a save, on Moritz Seider, and 12 minutes in, shots favored the Devils, 11-1.

Arvidsson looked like he would make something happen on a rush in the second half of the first period, driving the puck to the net through traffic but his shot went wide. Shots were 16-2 to the Devils when Finnie blasted out of the neutral zone and down the left flank, extending his stick to corral the puck Brandsegg-Nygard had sent into the zone, firing a shot that went in off the far post and made it 1-1 at 18:35. Anton Johansson earned his first career NHL point with the second assist. The Wings had three shots to New Jersey's 15 after 20 minutes.

The Wings came into the game averaging 32.8 shots per game, but only two goals. They made them count against the Devils, going up 2-1 on their fourth shot of the night. This time it was Finnie who found Brandsegg-Nygard with a pass across the slot, and Brandsegg-Nygard finishing the play when he ripped the puck from just inside the left circle for his second goal of the season.

The Wings grabbed momentum, only to give it back soon after. Dawson Mercer fired a pass across the ice and straight to Mantha, who was wide open with Justin Faulk trying to gap up and had time and space to make it 2-2 at 7:03 of the second period. Faulk was on the ice again during a penalty kill when Nico Hischier made short work of both him and Albert Johansson to be in position at the top of the crease to convert and make it 3-2, at 10:16.

DeBrincat became the third on the line to score, firing a shot from just inside the blue line and using Brandseg-Nygard as a screen, but again the momentum was short lived. A furious scramble by the net was saved when John Gibson pushed his right skate against the post, preventing anyone from poking it any further, only for Jesper Bratt to take advantage of a screened Gibson to make it 4-3 at 16:52, a minute and a half after DeBrincat's goals.

The Philadelphia Flyers on Thursday (7:30 p.m., ESPN+).

articles.title: Jack Hughes scores on a breakaway in OT, lifts Devils to a 5-4 win over Red Wings
articles.summary: DETROIT (AP) — Jack Hughes scored on a breakaway off a slick pass from Jesper Bratt early in overtime, lifting the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 win over the De...
articles.body:
DETROIT (AP) — Jack Hughes scored on a breakaway off a slick pass from Jesper Bratt early in overtime, lifting the New Jersey Devils to a 5-4 win over the Detroit Red Wings on Tuesday night.

New Jersey's Evan Rodrigues, Nico Hischier and Bratt scored tiebreaking goals and Anthony Mantha had a tying goal. Jake Allen stopped 22 shots for the Devils.

Alex DeBrincat had a pair of tying goals after Emmitt Finne and Michael Brandsegg-Nygard scored to give the Red Wings a 2-1 lead.

Detroit's John Gibson made 32 saves, including a kick save that denied Arseny Gritsyuk on an odd-man rush late in regulation to send the game to overtime.

The Red Wings got off to a rough start, getting outshot 16-0 midway through the first period. New Jersey, though, didn't take full advantage as Rodrigues scored its only goal in the opening period.

Finne scored on Detroit's third shot with 1:25 left in the first period and Brandsegg-Nygard scored on the team's next shot early in the second period.

The Devils, hoping to get back to the playoffs after finishing seventh in the division last year, acquired Rodrigues in a trade and signed Mantha — a former Red Wing — in free agency to boost their third line.

Detroit, meanwhile, had a shaky offseason.

Dylan Larkin asked to be traded and the former captain is still on the team. Simon Edvinsson , a standout defenseman, remains unsigned as a restricted free agent.

Devils forward Luke Evangelista was out with an illness after feeling worse throughout the game Monday night against Ottawa and was replaced by Stefan Noesen. New Jersey defenseman Johnathan Kovacevic made his season debut after missing all of training camp recovering from knee surgery this past spring.

Devils: Host the New York Rangers on Thursday night.

Red Wings: Host Philadelphia on Thursday night.

articles.title: Jury returns mixed verdict in Tyreek Hill civil battery case, awards $500,000 to ex-wife
articles.summary: Hill lost on two counts, won as to the rest.
articles.body:
The civil lawsuit brought by Tyreek Hill's ex-wife alleging multiple counts of battery and related legal claims has resulted in a verdict. Via Diana Moskovitz of Defector Media , the jury found Hill responsible for two counts of battery . He was found not responsible on the remaining counts.

The jury awarded Keeta Vaccaro $500,000 in compensatory damages. The jury did not enter an award of punitive damages.

The jury's decision not to award punitive damages is curious. Battery is an intentional tort. In Florida, however, the law requires " clear and convincing evidence " of intentional misconduct. It's possible, in theory, that the jury found evidence of battery under the lower "preponderance of the evidence" standard but not "clear and convincing" proof, which is a higher bar.

The outcome becomes relevant to the NFL's ongoing Personal Conduct Policy review arising from the allegations Vaccaro initially made against Hill in a divorce filing. The findings represent a neutral determination that Hill more likely than not committed battery, twice. However, the Personal Conduct Policy does not automatically subject a player to discipline based solely on a civil verdict; the league will still need to perform its own investigation and reach a conclusion through the collectively-bargained process.

Regardless, the finding of two instances of civil battery, plus a $500,000 verdict, could cause one or more potentially interested teams to refrain from pursuing him. Especially since the league could still find that Hill violated the policy as to the two incidents on which Hill lost — and all incidents on which he prevailed.

articles.title: Rams OLB Myles Garrett won't return to practice this week
articles.summary: The Rams will have to wait at least another week to have Myles Garrett back at practice.
articles.body:
Myles Garrett is eligible to come off injured reserve at any time after missing the last four games, but he still needs more time to recover from knee surgery. Los Angeles Rams head coach Sean McVay confirmed on Tuesday that Garrett will not return to practice this week, meaning he will not come off IR just yet.

The Rams can open Garrett's 21-day practice window whenever they'd like, but if they do so, he will need to be activated off IR within those three weeks. Ian Rapoport of NFL Network said Tuesday that his understanding is it's a six-week recovery for Garrett, which would put him in line to return in Week 7.

McVay has not yet confirmed when Garrett will be back for Los Angeles, but the team will not rush him back – and understandably so. It's a long season, so the Rams want to make sure he's available down the stretch.

Garrett has played just one game this season, and even in that contest, he wasn't 100% healthy. He said as much after the Rams' season opener, admitting it was the worst version of himself that he could've put out there.

A few days after that loss to the 49ers, Garrett underwent knee surgery, which landed him on injured reserve.

In Garrett's place, the Rams have used Byron Young and Josaiah Stewart heavily, with Wesley Bailey and Desjuan Johnson backing them up. They've survived Garrett's absence, but they can't wait to get their prized offseason addition back in the lineup.

articles.title: Desert Ridge football controversy. Here's what we know
articles.summary: Desert Ridge High School football kicked the starting quarterback off the team last week. Then, 12 teammates were suspended.
articles.body:
Mesa Desert Ridge football coach Miles Smith kicked starting quarterback Gunner Brewer off the team last week. Then, 12 teammates supporting him were suspended .

According to the quarterback's mom, Brewer was dismissed from the team for changing a play given to him to run in a 14-12 win at Vail Cienega on Oct. 2. He was told by Smith, she said, on that Monday, Oct. 5, that he felt disrespected and that he was no longer part of the team.

Two days later, the team was brought together to discuss Brewer's dismissal. Offensive lineman Will Stark, according to his mom, stood up and asked who wanted to see their quarterback back. A large group raised their hand.

Shadow Ridge flag football team defeats Desert Ridge

Kristie Stark, Will's mom, said an assistant coach told them that if they didn't like their decision, they could leave. Twelve players left. They were subsequently suspended from the team. Their banners were removed and equipment taken out of their lockers, she said. Athletic director Kevin Swann, after meeting with players and coaches, sent a letter to the Desert Ridge parents, detailing his findings.

The players came to the Friday, Oct. 9, home game in a show of support. They tried to help with the inflatable Jaguar that the players run through before games, but were turned away, according to a parent. They sat in the stands, while Desert Ridge lost to Mesa Red Mountain, 49-7.

Kristie Stark and her son met with Swann and Smith on Monday, Oct. 12, at which time they were informed that Will would no longer be part of the team through the rest of the season. In a voice message left to a parent on Monday, Oct. 12, athletic director Kevin Swann said that the players, seven of whom were underclassmen, were suspended for the rest of the season but could return for winter workouts and for next season.

On Tuesday, Kristie Stark met with the principal, Scott Smith. She told The Republic in a text message, "Just had a GREAT conversation with the school principal. Very receptive." Stark couldn't immediately be reached after the text message.

articles.summary: Springfield head coach Chris Wallace was excited to be in attendance. Getting to hear his team be announced Tuesday, Oct. 13, alongside other prominent state...
articles.body:
Springfield head coach Chris Wallace was excited to be in attendance.

Getting to hear his team be announced Tuesday, Oct. 13, alongside other prominent state and national basketball programs as a participant in the upcoming 24th annual Flyin' To The Hoop event at Trent Arena left the first-year head coach all smiles about the state of his team.

"We're not a flash in the pan team. We got some great freshman and great sophomores, and it's the sophomores that are going to really contribute," Wallace said. "We are going to be a tough out, and we're going to be exciting to watch. I think Springfield basketball is definitely back."

The Wildcats will be one of 30 teams playing at FTTH this season. It will be Springfield's first appearance since 2020.

Other Dayton-area teams selected to play are Alter, Bellbrook, Centerville, Chaminade Julienne, Fairmont, Northridge, Valley View and Wayne.

The four-day event will be held as typical during Martin Luther King Holiday weekend from Jan. 15-18, 2027.

Bellbrook, Centerville, Fairmont are matched with some of the top teams coming in from out of state. Alter and CJ will play a Greater Catholic League Co-Ed game against one another. Northridge, Valley View and Wayne get to test themselves against other outstanding teams from Ohio.

As of Tuesday's announcement, there are six 5-star prospects and 29 others rated as 4-stars that will appear at FTTH. Asa Montgomery, a 5-star committed to Duke that plays at Hillgrove (Ga.), is ranked eighth overall in the 247Sports composite rankings for the class of 2027 and is the highest-rated recruit in the country set to appear.

Other notable recruits set to play are Pickerington Central's Landon Evans, a 3-star who committed to Wright State in July, and Xavier-commit Brandon Mason Jr., a 4-star who plays at Link Academy (Mo.)

The schedule will follow similar trends as used in recent years.

The Friday night slate has several national teams featuring multiple top prospects. Local teams begin Saturday and are interspersed with matchups against Ohio and other national teams. The event concludes Monday with host Fairmont's game and a small school showcase.

"We're going to have 11 of the top-20 Ohio teams regardless of their division," FTTH president Eric Horstman said. "We're going to have some of the top national teams. There's some stories behind some of them, there is a reason why you see these. You might not recognize the name right away, but there's a reason why they're coming to this event."

Centerville will be making its 21st appearance at FTTH. The Elks have participated more than any other school. Wayne is next on the list and is back on the schedule for the 20th consecutive event.

"When we show up, everything is first class. The way you're treated, the way the players are treated, how organized everything is, everything stays on time," Wayne head coach Nathan Martindale said. "We truly believe this is the number one showcase event in the country."

The 2027 event will be the first time Flyin' To The Hoop utilizes a shot clock for all contests. The move was approved by the Ohio High School Basketball Coaches Association in August and joins a list of 19 events in Ohio allowed to have a shot clock.

Two teams from the Nike EYBL Scholastic League will be playing: CIA Bella Vista out of Arizona, and Link Academy from Missouri. Both will play two games, including one against one another on Saturday.

Flyin' To The Hoop entered into a partnership with the national prep league beginning with last year's event.

articles.title: 'Never say no to Big Woo': Could Brandon Woodruff pitch in a World Series?
articles.summary: With the Brewers two wins away from the World Series, Brandon Woodruff threw a high-intent bullpen at Dodger Stadium
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES – As Brandon Woodruff brought his glove set in front of his face and gripped the ball with his right hand in the bullpen beyond the right-field fence at Dodger Stadium, there was far more intent in his eyes than the standard off-day bullpen that he's thrown hundreds of times in his career.

For 31 pitches as the Milwaukee Brewers worked out on an off-day Oct. 13, Woodruff stared down the mitt, oftentimes muttering bits of self-talk into the glove.

"For me, I'm not really holding back," said the right-hander. "I'm going as hard as my body will let me right now. It's just where we're at with everything."

That Woodruff and the Brewers are even here – weighing the 33-year-old as an option for a potential World Series roster – to begin with feels somewhat like a far-fetched reality.

Less than two months ago, the public expectation was Woodruff would be undergoing a second shoulder surgery, a procedure that put him ever pitching in the major leagues again in question. Woodruff revealed in late August he, it turned out out, didn't need surgery. And not only that, he and the Brewers weren't ruling out a return in the postseason.

With Milwaukee ahead two games to none as the National League Championship Series shifts to Los Angeles for three games, Woodruff threw his first high-intent bullpen since resuming a throwing program in early September (he threw a light touch-and-feel off the mound two days prior).

"What I set out to do was to be able to have a shot to do it," Woodruff said. "It's one of those things that it's hard to process that can happen.

"If it does happen, the competitive juices take over and I'm not worried about this [being] my first time pitching in a major-league game in three months. I'm not looking at that. I'm looking at today.

"We'll just see what happens, but if I have the opportunity I'll be ready to go."

The next step for Woodruff is to face live hitters, which could happen as soon as this weekend if he recovers well from his bullpen. That phase will be critical for the Brewers as they weigh the decision of placing him on a possible World Series roster – and all the implications that come with that.

"We'll have to see live BPs and stuff like that," said pitching coach Jim Henderson. "Just make sure he's progressing. The biggest thing is his health and his future. And if it happens to line up with him pitching this season, then great.

"I think we have to be aware of where the team's at, be aware of where he's at. If it works, it works. We're not going to force it or put pressure on it. But if it does, he's also performed really really well when he's on the mound.

"So it's never a question of whether we want him out there. We do. It's a matter of lining it up."

What, realistically, would the Brewers need to see from Woodruff to go from not pitching since July 4 to using a World Series roster spot on him?

"It's probably going to be based on his health and strength and velo," Henderson said. "That's going to be a big determining factor."

Woodruff's velocity in the bullpen session wasn't zipping in the mid-90s, but the Brewers also don't necessarily need it to be where it was when Woodruff was healthy this year.

Their brass has seen him throw in the upper-80s in side sessions and rehab assignments only to ramp it up in-game each of the last two years. Whether he has the ability to do that this time and coming off of this injury is something Henderson, pitching coach Chris Hook, manager Pat Murphy and the front office will have to decide, but having seen it happen before seems to bring about confidence given the adrenaline that would come with a Fall Classic stage.

And speaking of confidence, the Brewers have plenty of that in Woodruff's execution – so much so that a World Series comeback is entirely possible largely because of that trust.

"I think his execution's going to be there," Henderson said. "He's always been a high executor, even when he was going through the stuff earlier this year. I don't think execution's going to be a problem."

Still, Woodruff's stuff would almost certainly need to reach a certain threshold for this to actually take place. So, where is Woodruff's stuff at right now?

"If you ask me, it's pretty good," he said.

The plot, as Murphy likes to say, thickens. Considering the Brewers haven't used three pitchers in their bullpen at all through six postseason games – a point to which Murphy said before the workout that "this isn't tryouts – it's not as if there's no way to make room for him on the roster.

"It's a nice little piece to this," Henderson said. "You'll never say no to 'Big Woo' out there."

articles.body: Naomi Osaka wanted the French Open to take athletes’ mental health more seriously. In May 2021, the tennis star announced that she would skip mandatory news conferences because of the pressure they placed on players. She also hoped the fines for missing those appearances would support mental health charities. What began as a protest over media duties soon became a much bigger conversation about the cost of competing at the highest level.The French Open fined Osaka $15,000 on May 30, 2021, after she skipped a news conference following her first-round win. A day later, she withdrew from the tournament after officials warned of harsher penalties. Osaka’s decision brought fresh attention to the pressure athletes face away from competition and her request to turn the fine into support for mental health. Naomi Osaka wanted her $15,000 French Open fine to support mental healthBefore the tournament, Osaka explained her decision in a social media statement. She wrote, “I’ve often felt that people have no regard for athletes’ mental health and this rings very true whenever I see a press conference or partake in one.”The statement, shared ahead of the 2021 French Open, explained why she wanted to step away from news conferences. Osaka said players often faced repeated questions and comments that could create doubt. She did not want to keep putting herself through an experience she felt could harm her well-being.She also questioned the policy of forcing players to choose between media appearances and financial penalties. In the same statement, Osaka described the idea of telling athletes to “do press or be fined” while ignoring their mental health as “laughable.”Her request went beyond avoiding the penalty. Osaka expressed hope that the money she received as fines for skipping media duties would go to a mental health charity. That gave her protest a clear purpose: she wanted the issue to lead to support for people who needed it.However, the tournament authorities stood by their media requirements. On May 30, 2021, officials fined Osaka $15,000 for missing her post-match news conference after beating Patricia Maria Tig in the first round. The four Grand Slam tournaments then issued a joint statement warning that continued refusals could bring harsher penalties, including possible suspension from future events.Osaka withdrew from the French Open on May 31 rather than continue the dispute. Naomi Osaka’s French Open withdrawal put athlete mental health in the spotlightIn her withdrawal statement on May 31, Osaka explained that the situation had developed differently from what she expected. She wrote, “I never wanted to be a distraction.”She also spoke about her mental health struggles, revealing that she had experienced bouts of depression since the 2018 US Open and had dealt with social anxiety. Osaka said she would take time away from the court.Her announcement changed the conversation around the $15,000 fine. The dispute was no longer just about a player's obligation to speak to reporters. It also raised questions about how tennis could enforce media rules while recognising the personal pressures athletes face.Osaka’s proposed donation was an important part of that message. She wanted the money connected to the dispute to support mental health care rather than remain a punishment with no wider purpose. However, her stated wish to donate the fine money does not confirm that tournament officials ultimately gave it to a charity.The episode also highlighted a difficult balance in professional sport. Grand Slam organisers expect players to meet media obligations, while athletes must manage the demands of competition and public scrutiny. Osaka’s decision challenged tennis officials to consider how those responsibilities could coexist.Her withdrawal did not settle the debate, but it ensured that athlete mental health received attention beyond the court. articles.summary: Simone Biles knows what it feels like to grow up without a stable family environment.
articles.body: Simone Biles knows what it feels like to grow up without a stable family environment. The Olympic gymnastics champion spent part of her childhood in foster care before her grandparents adopted her. After years, that experience gave her a personal reason to support kids facing similar struggles. Back in 2022, her partnership with cybersecurity company Axonius helped Friends of the Children receive a $50,000 gift, giving the nonprofit more aid for its work with young people.Biles used her public platform to bring attention to an organisation that offers children long-term mentorship. Her involvement continued into 2023, when she helped spotlight the charity through a campaign, a magazine feature and an event in her hometown of Spring, Texas.How Simone Biles used her foster care experience to support childrenBiles has never hidden why the cause feels personal to her. On March 7, 2023, Friends of the Children shared her comments from a People magazine feature.“I was a foster kid, so I know how hard it is to feel like no one’s there,” Biles said in the feature. “Those young people will always have a piece of my heart, which is why Friends of the Children is so dear to me.”Biles entered foster care in Ohio when she was three. Her maternal grandfather, Ron Biles, and his wife, Nellie, later adopted Simone and her younger sister, Adria, when Simone was six.That past helped shape her connection with Friends of the Children, a nonprofit that pairs kids with professional mentors who support them over the long term. Biles began working with the organisation in 2020 and took part in virtual activities with children in its programmes. How Axonius’ $50,000 gift helped expand the charity’s reachThe financial support came through Biles’ partnership with Axonius. In February 2023, she featured Friends of the Children in a commercial for the cybersecurity company. The nonprofit later confirmed in its November 14, 2023, announcement that Axonius had provided a $50,000 gift after Biles highlighted its work.The partnership also helped the organisation reach more families. In January 2023, Biles hosted a Breakfast of Champions event at her gym in Spring, Texas, to celebrate a limited-edition Wheaties box featuring her and the charity. The event also marked the launch of Friends of the Children’s Houston chapter.Biles continued to advocate for the organisation that year. On May 16, 2023, she joined more than 100 young people from its programmes on a Zoom call for National Foster Care Month and Mental Health Awareness Month.In Biles' case, the work goes beyond a single donation or campaign. articles.title: Brady Tkachuk Makes NHL History with Hat Trick on 3 Assists From Brother Matthew in Panthers' Win
articles.summary: The Tkachuk brothers made NHL history in a Tuesday night win over the Columbus Blue Jackets.
articles.body:
The Tkachuk brothers made NHL history in a Tuesday night win over the Columbus Blue Jackets.

Brady Tkachuk scored three consecutive goals, on which Matthew Tkachuk registered three assists, in the Florida Panthers' 7-3 victory.

He is the first player in NHL history to have his brother assist on every goal of a natural hat trick, according to NHL PR.

Brady is also the ninth player in NHL history to have his brother set up three goals of a hat trick, and the first since Daniel Sedin scored on three helpers from Henrik Sedin in 2015, according to the NHL .

The Panthers were trailing 1-0 in Columbus when Brady recorded the third-fastest hat trick in franchise history in just over eight minutes of the second period.

His initial goal marked the first time the Tkachuk brothers had combined for a tally since playing for Team USA during the 2026 Milan Cortina Olympics.

Brady is the eighth Panthers player to record a natural hat trick, and the first since Matthew in 2024.

The Tkachuk brothers both assisted on a Carter Verhaeghe goal later in the second frame. Matthew set a franchise record for assists in a single period with the helper.

Matthew also assisted on a goal from Sam Reinhart early in the third period. He (0-5—5) and Brady (3-1—4) finished the game as the first pair of brothers and teammates since the Sedin twins in 2015 to combine for nine points in a single game.

Brady had recorded just a single assist through his first six games with Matthew and the Panthers prior to his four-point outing Tuesday night.

"For sure, felt that pressure... felt like I wasn't doing my job, and wasn't good enough, but knew eventually it was going to come," Brady told ESPN after the Panthers' win.

Brady's best night as a Panther came at a crucial time for a franchise that had dropped four of its last five games while losing key players including Aleksander Barkov and Brad Marchand to injury.

The Panthers (3-2-2) will hope to see more production from the Tkachuk brothers as Barkov and Marchand continue recovering from injuries expected to sideline each player for at least the next month.

articles.title: Brady Takchuk Picks Up Hat Trick, Matthew Tkachuk Logs Five Assists As Panthers Dominate In Columbus
articles.summary: A historic second-period surge saw the Tkachuk siblings rewrite record books as Brady’s natural hat trick fueled a blowout victory during a masterclass of fa...
articles.body:
Brady Tkachuk broke out of his early season scoring slump in a big way this week.

After picking up his first point as a member of the Florida Panthers on Monday in Buffalo, assisting on a power play goal by Sam Reinhart, the younger Tkachuk brother took things to another level Tuesday night in Columbus.

In the span of all of 8:03 during the second period, Tkachuk scored not one, not two, but three goals, helping the Panthers to a resounding 7-3 victory over the Blue Jackets at Nationwide Arena.

Brady's first goal came off a high end play by his brother, as Matthew jumped off the ice and snagged a clearing attempt by Carson Soucy with his glove before feeding Brady cutting down the slot.

His wrist shot sailed past Cam Talbot's blocker and into the top of the net, tying the game 1-1 just 2:27 into the middle frame.

"It was a great play by Matthew to kind of get the ball rolling there, and I just wanted to keep going and I thought we got better and better as the game went on," said Brady.

Florida went on their first power play of the game a couple minutes later, and once again it was Brady Tkachuk who would capitalize on the opportunity.

This time, the puck found its way from below the goal line to the point, where Seth Jones wound up for a slapshot but instead turned his body and slap-passed the puck to Matthew Tkachuk along the half boards.

Matthew corralled the pass and looked towards the net, capturing the attention of Talbot before sliding a cross-ice pass toward the slot. That's where Brady was waiting with his stick blade on the ice to deflect the pass into the net behind Talbot, who couldn't get back after committing toward Matthew in the right circle.

The hat trick was completed just four and a half minutes later.

Once again, Florida was on the power play.

A pretty passing sequence saw the puck quickly travel from Brady to Jones to Matthew, who then sent a touch pass toward Reinhart in the slot.

Reinhart's shot went just wide of the near post, but the puck took a hard bounce off the back boards and came out the other side of the net.

Seeing this develop, Brady quickly charged toward the far post and got his stick on the puck before Talbot could react, picking up his third goal of the period.

The hat trick was the fourth of Brady's career, his first since March of 2024, and obviously his first as a member of the Panthers.

It was also the first natural hat trick in NHL history where the goal-scorer's brother assisted on all three goals, according to the league.

"There's some chemistry there," said Panthers head coach Paul Maurice. "He and his brother played together their whole lives as kids, and there's something there for sure."

Before the period ended, both Tkachuk brothers assisted on a goal by Carter Verhaeghe, and then Matthew picked up a fifth helper when Sam Reinhart netted his first of two goals during the final frame.

Overall on the night, four of Matthew's five assists came while Florida was on the power play, as did two of Brady's goals.

"Our power play struggled for a little bit," said Panthers head coach Paul Maurice. "It just needed something to go, and it did for them."

Matthew now has points in six straight games, while he and Brady combined to make some Panthers history, tying a record for most points in a period, with four apiece.

So after starting the season with no points in his first five games, Brady is now up to three goals and five points through seven games, which seems much more respectable.

It might be a good idea for Marice to keep the Tkachuk brothers on the same line, considering Matthew has been on the ice for every one of Brady's points over the past couple days.

For now, we can just sit back enjoy watching Matthew and Brady thrive while playing together.

"It's pretty cool," Brady said. "It's something that, of course, you've always dreamed of happening."

articles.title: Sidney Crosby's $104.4 million contract changed his career finances, but the full story goes far beyond hockey
articles.summary: Sidney Crosby’s career earnings reflect more than two decades of elite hockey and a long-standing relationship with the Pittsburgh Penguins.
articles.body: Sidney Crosby’s career earnings reflect more than two decades of elite hockey and a long-standing relationship with the Pittsburgh Penguins. His 12-year, $104.4 million contract, signed in 2012, gave him long-term financial security and helped shape his standing among the NHL’s highest-paid players. Yet his estimated net worth is not simply a reflection of that deal. Endorsements, commercial partnerships and the distinction between salary earned and wealth accumulated all help explain his financial position. Crosby has built his reputation on the ice, but understanding his fortune requires looking beyond his contract.Sidney Crosby's $104.4 million deal set the foundationCrosby signed the contract in July 2012, committing to Pittsburgh for 12 years. The deal carried an average annual value of $8.7 million, a figure tied to his August 7 birthday and No. 87 jersey. It was a major commitment from the Penguins, but the investment paid off in ways that went beyond the team's books. Crosby helped Pittsburgh win Stanley Cup titles in 2016 and 2017, adding to the championship he had already secured in 2009.The contract also gave Crosby a degree of financial stability that few players enjoy across such a long stretch of their careers. He remained with one franchise, avoiding the uncertainty that often comes with changing teams and negotiating new deals. His earnings continued to grow, and in September 2024, he agreed to a two-year, $17.4 million extension that keeps him in Pittsburgh through the 2026-27 season.Endorsements added another layer to his earningsCrosby's income has never depended on hockey contracts alone. His reputation made him an attractive partner for brands looking to reach fans beyond the rink. Forbes reported in 2012 that he earned about $4 million annually from endorsements, including partnerships with Reebok, Tim Hortons, Bell Canada and Gatorade. The same report placed his total earnings at $12.7 million for that year, counting both his playing salary and commercial deals.That commercial appeal lasted well beyond his early years in the league. Crosby later worked with Adidas and other established brands, building a profile that reached consumers outside the core hockey audience. His marketability rested on more than trophies. He was a familiar face in a sport where star power can be harder to translate into mainstream recognition than in basketball or football.These deals help explain why his earning power has remained strong over time. They also show why a player's financial picture cannot be measured by his NHL contract alone. Endorsement income adds to gross earnings, though taxes, spending and other financial obligations affect how much of that money ultimately becomes personal wealth.Why is Sidney Crosby's estimated net worth lower than his career earnings?Celebrity Net Worth estimates Crosby's fortune at $75 million, while its career earnings breakdown lists approximately $158.9 million in NHL salary. Those figures measure different things. Career earnings track money received over time, while net worth estimates what someone owns after accounting for liabilities. The two numbers should not be treated as interchangeable.The $75 million estimate is not a publicly audited account of Crosby's finances. His private investments, spending, taxes and other assets are not fully available for independent verification. That makes any precise claim about his wealth difficult to confirm, even when his contract history is well documented.Still, the broad picture is clear. Sidney Crosby has turned sustained success with Pittsburgh into more than $150 million in reported NHL salary earnings, backed by years of endorsement work. His 2012 contract was a defining part of that story, but it was not the whole story. articles.title: Walker Kessler debuts, but Luka Doncic sits during Lakers' preseason loss to Warriors
articles.summary: Walker Kessler makes his Lakers debut and scores 11 points in a preseason loss to the Warriors on Tuesday night.
articles.body:
The plan for the Lakers had been to turn their fourth preseason game into a dress rehearsal for the upcoming season.

The Lakers did get the preseason debut of center Walker Kessler on Tuesday night, a good sign for them to see their biggest acquisition of the summer play.

But on the flip side, Luka Doncic didn't play in the Lakers' 101-89 loss to the Golden State Warriors at T-Mobile Arena because he was resting.

"He's not injured, just getting the night off," Lakers coach JJ Redick said.

So, it was left up to Kessler, Austin Reaves and the rest of the available Lakers to sort things out. And Reaves and Kessler were on point.

In just his second preseason game, Reaves was doing what is expected of him, scoring 28 points on 10-for-18 shooting, including four for seven on three-pointers, with seven assists and four rebounds. But forced to handle the ball more with Doncic out, Reaves also had seven turnovers.

Kessler started and had 11 points, nine rebounds, one blocked shot and one steal in 16 minutes.

For the Lakers, it was good to see Kessler on the court. They gave up a lot to acquire him in a trade with the Utah Jazz — two unprotected first-round picks and two pick swaps and then signing him to a four-year, $130-million contract.

Kessler played in only five games last season while recovering from a torn labrum in his left shoulder.

He missed the first three Lakers' preseason games because of a left pinky injury.

" Yeah, I mean it was a lot of fun being out there again," he said. "It's been so long. Before the game I was actually pretty nervous, to be honest. But, getting out there and just playing with the guys, it was a blast. I can't really, you know speak to ... I think I have a certain presence on the floor, but I think my teammates around me did a great job of playing defense on the perimeter. I think we shared the ball really well tonight. Just how it was, especially in the first half. It was a lot of fun."

He began his night with a defensive rebound, which allowed the Lakers to set up their offense early in the first quarter.

Kessler then cut to the basket, took a pass from Reaves and scored on a layup, his first points of the preseason.

His second basket was a left-handed layup early in the second quarter. Shortly after, Kessler blocked a shot by Warriors center Charles Bassey from behind, a display of his defensive presence.

Another good sign, less than a minute later, was when Kessler got an offensive rebound and bounded back up for a dunk.

When the Warriors went to their small-ball lineup in the first quarter, it meant the 7-foot-2 Kessler would be tested on defense, because his man was 6-2 Gary Payton II. It meant Kessler was forced to play defense on the perimeter and not down low where the Lakers prefer him.

While he was out and unable to play, Kessler learned a few things about himself.

"Yeah, I think what I missed most was competing," Kessler said. "Quite frankly, competing to win, and I think as far as making me a better basketball player, I just think it has made me long to go try to win every game and win every night. So returning, I think it makes me a little better basketball player."

The Lakers lost to the Warriors for the second time this preseason. Their other two games were victories over the Sacramento Kings. They play one more preseason game, Friday night against the Denver Nuggets at Crypto.com Arena, and then open the season against the Warriors at home on Oct. 21.

Before the game, Redick said the plan was for the Lakers to "continue to work on us."

"We have kind of circled this game, not as a full dress rehearsal, just in terms of our scout presentation, but we gave the guys a sample of that this morning and at shoot-ariund," Redick said. "Not as much game-planning necessarily, but just kind of the sequencing of how we present prior to a game. We'll do the same thing pregame with a brief personnel tape. We just want to get better. I mean, that's the biggest thing. We want to get healthy, we want to get better, we want to continue to build our fitness and cardio level and find a rhythm. And it's been a little disjointed with having some guys out."

Redick said rookie Cameron Carr, guard Collin Sexton (lower leg) and forwards Ziaire Williams (right foot contusion) and Adou Thiero (undisclosed) "are still day to day" with their injuries.

This story originally appeared in Los Angeles Times .

articles.title: Man City deserve to keep trophies despite charges, says PSG’s Luis Enrique
articles.summary: Enrique, a friend of former Man City boss Guardiola, hopes the club can avoid the sanction of losing its titles.
articles.body:
Paris St ‌‌Germain manager Luis Enrique says Manchester City were ⁠⁠deserving winners ⁠⁠of their trophies and should be allowed to keep them, despite the English club facing sanctions after ⁠⁠being found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules.

Enrique said on Tuesday that there was a need to “respect the ⁠⁠process and wait for the final decision” when asked about the verdict before PSG’s Champions League match against City .

“There are authorities responsible for making that decision, these decisions, and we have to wait, but if I ⁠⁠speak only about football and the things that I saw on the pitch, ⁠⁠Man City deserve those trophies,” the Spanish coach said, amid speculation that titles won during the charged period could be stripped.

City host PSG at the Etihad Stadium on Wednesday.

The Premier League said City had used “sham” commercial contracts as ⁠⁠part of schemes to inflate revenue and understate costs by more than 900 million pounds ($1.19bn).

City, who have denied wrongdoing throughout the case and have appealed the verdict, could face punishments ‌‌ranging from fines and a points deduction to relegation and potentially being stripped of their titles.

“I love ⁠⁠the way they play football, and after that, you have to wait [for the] last decision and nothing else. I hope they can ‌‌avoid ‌‌that sanction.”

Former City boss Pep Guardiola , who left the club in May, is set to return to the Etihad for the match against PSG.

Enrique is a close friend and former Barcelona teammate of Guardiola.

Enzo Maresca has so far made a flawless start to the daunting task of succeeding Guardiola.

The Italian has won all eight games in all competitions, but Enrique dismissed suggestions that Wednesday’s match is the chance to lay down an early marker for either side.

“January is when you can really see the team’s level,” he added. “Five or six months down the line, things are so different. Many teams change.

“But it’s an interesting match at this stage, a fun one to watch.”

articles.title: Asian Para Games: Defending champion Shailesh Kumar ready for another big jump
articles.summary: KOLKATA: There was a time when people in his village wondered what future awaited him.
articles.body: KOLKATA: There was a time when people in his village wondered what future awaited him.Unable to walk properly since childhood after being diagnosed with polio in his right leg, Shailesh Kumar, a resident of Islamnagar village in Bihar’s Jamui district, often faced doubts about what he could achieve.Today, the same people urge him to bring glory to the country, thanks to the success he has achieved in para-athletics. The T63 high jumper heads to the Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, as the defending champion, carrying not just expectations but also the confidence that comes from changing lives, including his own.“Life has changed significantly, both financially and socially. Earlier, people would wonder what I could achieve because I couldn’t walk properly. Today, their mindset has changed. They see that a para athlete can represent the country and achieve success,” Shailesh told TOI ahead of the Games.Since winning gold with a Games record at the 2023 Asian Para Games in China, the 26-year-old has added several major titles to his résumé, including gold medals at 2025 World Para Athletics Championships and 2026 World Para Athletics Grand Prix.Training under close friend and coach Ronak Malik in Bengaluru since Jan 2025, the 26-year-old is now focused on defending his high jump title.He enters the competition after overcoming knee issues that troubled him earlier in the season, but Malik is confident his ward can retain the gold medal in high jump and also contend for a podium finish in long jump.“If everything goes according to plan, he has the potential to win medals in both events. Gold is definitely a possibility. He has already set records at the World Championships and Asian Championships and has achieved personal best performances,” said Malik, a former national-level high jumper.Training a para athlete requires a different approach from coaching able-bodied athletes, and Malik regularly consults experienced jump coach GV Gaonkar to fine-tune Shailesh’s programme.While Malik’s guidance has proved hugely beneficial on the field, their friendship has also played a key role in Shailesh’s resurgence, particularly after Paris Paralympics, where he narrowly missed a medal and finished fourth.“After beginning his training in Sonipat in 2019, Shailesh moved to SAI Gandhinagar under coach Vinod Chauhan. Unfortunately, Vinod sir passed away in a road accident in April 2023. It was a difficult phase for Shailesh and he wasn’t in the best frame of mind going into the Paris Paralympics,” Malik said.It was after Chauhan’s death that Shailesh reconnected with Malik. Together, they are now targeting success not only at the Asian Para Games but also at next year’s World Championships and, ultimately, the Paralympics in LA.But as Malik says, none of it would have been possible without the discipline and dedication of Shailesh, who chose sport even as his family hoped he would focus on studies and secure a stable job.“People had different opinions about me, so I wanted to do something different. My family stood by me throughout and today they are very proud,” said Shailesh.But as he prepares for another Asian Para Games campaign, he remains determined not to be weighed down by expectations. “I am the defending champion, but I am an athlete first. When you represent the country there is pressure, but I try to keep it to a minimum and perform freely,” he said.For Shailesh, though, the biggest motivation remains the journey itself. articles.title: Strong defense helps Kerrville Tivy outlast Davenport in thrilling five-set win
articles.summary: Kerrville Tivy put on a stellar display of defense to rally from a deficit against Davenport and help the Antlers stay tied for first in a tough District 27-...
articles.body:
In what's essentially championship week for Kerrville Tivy, the Antlers passed a big road test on Tuesday with a 25-20, 23-25, 21-25, 25-15, 15-10 victory against Davenport in a matchup of state-ranked teams.

The Antlers (25-14), ranked No. 8 in Class 4A, earned a District 27-4A sweep against No. 5 Davenport (29-10). Tivy also prevailed in five sets against the Wolves on Sept. 25. The Antlers moved to 3-0 against Davenport this season, which includes a two-set tournament win.

That sets up a showdown for first place on Friday when Wimberley comes to town.

Tivy senior setter Rylie Coates had career-best 52 assists to go with 12 digs, six kills, two aces and two blocks. Senior Karlynn Way led the team with 15 kills. Senior Danica Blaker and senior Jilian Stebbins each had 12 kills. Senior Lily Gonzalez had 10 kills.

The Antlers frustrated the Wolves by keeping the ball in play and buying extra chances to get points. Brooke Bailey led the Antlers with 19 digs, followed by Rylan Adams (14), Lauren Holland (13) and Blaker (11).

"It's great when our back row can get the crazy balls up, and it just helps us a lot because we can run our offense and get good plays off our defense," Way said.

That fits exactly what they've done this season. Entering Tuesday's match, the Antlers had five players with between 189 to 293 digs.

"We work defense all the time in practice," Blaker said. "We have a ton of different things that we work on, like our positioning. It's definitely something we kill and drill."

That means more opportunities for Coates to set the ball. She had 1,061 assists entering the match, which was ranked No. 8 in the state. She has now reached 50 assists three times this season.

"She's definitely a big team leader on the court," Way said. "She is very good at rotating the ball and giving all our hitters a chance to hit the ball."

Entering Tuesday there was a three-way tie for first place in district with Tivy, Davenport and No. 6 Wimberley at 5-1. Tivy is now tied with Wimberley for first at 6-1 following the Texans' sweep of Fredericksburg on Tuesday. The Antlers host Wimberley (38-4) on Friday.

In district play, the Antlers are thriving with an experienced team (12 seniors) that moved from Class 5A to 4A this season. Coates said that factors into the hustle they show on defense.

"We understand that these are some of our last games together," Coates said. "Since we've been playing with each other since sixth grade, everything matters so much to us. Not just from a volleyball standpoint, but from a family standpoint. Every extended rally just means so much more."

Tivy took control of the first set with a 9-1 run, mostly behind the serving of Brooke Bailey, to grab a 17-11 lead. The Antlers kept a comfortable cushion of the rest of the set.

Davenport took a 2-1 lead in sets by holding off strong Tivy runs. In the second set, the Wolves led 18-13 before the Antlers tied it at 19 and then at 23. Davenport locked it up with a kill by junior McKenzie Myers and an ace by junior Kylie Dahl that landed uncontested in the far left corner.

In the third set, the Wolves erased a 12-6 deficit before taking a 21-15 lead. Tivy cut it to 22-20 following a kill by Way, but the Wolves secured it with kills by Myers and Aliyah Beauford.

Tivy evened it thanks to a fast start in the fourth set, jumping to a 6-1 lead after back-to-back aces from Gonzalez. Davenport cut it to 10-8 with a Myers kill, but the Antlers responded with an 11-3 run.

The fifth set was tight early until the Antlers pulled away with a 6-1 run to end it.

The Los Angeles Lakers have been very cautious with Walker Kessler , their marquee offseason acquisition, during preseason, holding him out for their first three exhibition contests. Kessler had been dealing with a finger injury, but head coach JJ Redick wasn't very concerned and made sure to say that he'll be suiting up in at least one preseason game.

The 25-year-old center did just that on Tuesday as the Lakers faced the Golden State Warriors for the second time in preseason. Not only did Kessler play, he also impressed in his 16 minutes on the floor. He recorded 11 points and nine rebounds, to go along with one assist, one steal, and one block each, and he made four of his six shot attempts on the night. Moreover, the Lakers outscored the Warriors by 15 during his time on the court. (LA ended up losing the game, 101-89.)

Suffice to say, this was enough to impress head coach JJ Redick , who knows just how impactful Kessler will be for the Lakers this upcoming season.

articles.title: Warriors rookie Yaxel Lendeborg involved in injury scare during Lakers preseason game
articles.summary: The Golden State Warriors had a brief scare on Tuesday night when rookie Yaxel Lendeborg appeared to hurt his ankle during their preseason game against the L...
articles.body:
The Golden State Warriors had a brief scare on Tuesday night when rookie Yaxel Lendeborg appeared to hurt his ankle during their preseason game against the Los Angeles Lakers at T-Mobile Arena in Las Vegas.

Lendeborg turned his left ankle on a drive to the basket and was visibly hobbled afterward. He stayed in the game long enough to shoot his two free throws, but he was checked on right after and headed into the tunnel toward the locker room for further evaluation.

Given how the ankle looked, there was immediate concern that the 23-year-old would not return. Instead, it turned out to be a false alarm . Lendeborg was back on the floor shortly after, subbing back into the game following his quick trip to the locker room.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

He looked none the worse for wear, either. Lendeborg finished with 17 points on 5-of-11 shooting, including 6-of-9 from the free-throw line, to go with five rebounds, four assists and two steals in 26 minutes.

That avoided what could have been a significant setback for Golden State. The Warriors selected Lendeborg with the No. 11 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft after a decorated college career. He was a two-time AAC Defensive Player of the Year at UAB before transferring to Michigan, where he was named Big Ten Player of the Year and a consensus first-team All-American while helping the Wolverines win the national championship.

He has wasted little time making an impression in the preseason. In his home debut against the Lakers on Oct. 6 , Lendeborg posted 17 points and nine rebounds while shooting 7-of-11 from the field in a 124-98 rout at Chase Center.

Tuesday's rematch featured short-handed rosters on both sides. The Lakers rested Luka Doncic and were without Collin Sexton, Ziaire Williams, Adou Thiero and Cameron Carr, while Walker Kessler made his preseason debut after missing time with a finger injury . Golden State, meanwhile, played without Jimmy Butler and Moses Moody.

Lendeborg has quickly become a big part of the Warriors' plans, and his versatility has opened up new lineup options. Seeing him jog back onto the floor after the ankle tweak was a welcome sight for a team that is counting on him to make an immediate impact.
