articles.title: Lakers vs. Warriors: Kessler’s debut, Reaves’ big night and second-half struggles
articles.summary: Walker Kessler impressed in his Lakers debut and Austin Reaves scored 28 points, but 30 turnovers and a second-half collapse led to a 101-89 loss to the Warr...
articles.body:
LAS VEGAS — Walker Kessler was nervous before his first game with the Los Angeles Lakers. Once he got on the floor Tuesday, he gave them an encouraging look at what their new center can provide.

Kessler finished with 11 points, nine rebounds, an assist, a steal and a block in 16 minutes during the Lakers' 101-89 preseason loss to the Warriors at T-Mobile Arena.

Austin Reaves led the way with 28 points, seven assists and four rebounds in 25 minutes while Luka Dončić rested. The Lakers built a 20-point lead before their offense stalled, committing 29 turnovers and falling to 2-2 in the preseason.

Sandro Mamukelashvili continued his strong preseason with 10 points and seven rebounds, while Quentin Grimes contributed nine points and six assists.

After missing the first three exhibitions with a jammed left pinkie, Kessler quickly contributed around the basket.

He collected a defensive rebound early, scored his first basket off a pass from Reaves and later added a powerful two-handed putback dunk.

"It was a lot of fun being out there again. It's been so long," Kessler said. "Before the game I was actually pretty nervous, but getting out there and just playing with the guys, it was a blast."

His activity reflected a message he and coach JJ Redick established for the season: Be relentless.

For Kessler, that means pursuing rebounds, running the floor and staying consistently involved on both ends.

"JJ and I talked, and that's what we came up with this year: relentless," Kessler said. "And for me, that means just crashing every time, trying to be a presence in the paint, outside, run [and] play hard. Don't take plays off on the offensive, defensive end. So, that's gonna be my goal for this year."

Redick saw that approach translate during Kessler's first-half minutes.

"I think he's a great fit for our team," Redick said. "I thought he did a nice job of running the floor, crashing, had some terrific rebounds in traffic, protected the rim. Just [a] really, really good first half from him."

His debut demonstrated how his finishing and rebounding can help, but his minutes alongside Dončić will have to wait.

With Dončić (rest) out with a non-injury, Reaves handled the primary scoring and playmaking responsibilities, shooting 10 of 18 from the field and four of seven from 3-point range.

He helped the Lakers establish control before halftime, creating his own opportunities while developing an early connection with Kessler. The center's movement toward the basket gave Reaves a target and forced Golden State to account for both players.

"He was really good in the minutes he had," Reaves said. "He's gonna continue to get better every single game."

Reaves' production was encouraging in his second preseason appearance. His seven turnovers, however, also contributed to a problem that continued as the Lakers changed lineups.

The Lakers outscored Golden State 63-50 in the first half and extended their advantage to 20 early in the third quarter.

The Warriors would go on to outscore L.A. 51-26 in the second half, turning a double-digit deficit into a 12-point victory.

With Kessler finished for the night and Reaves playing limited minutes after the break, the Lakers struggled to organize their offense. They scored just 13 points in each of the final two quarters.

Golden State generated 26 points off of the Lakers turnovers, repeatedly benefiting from possessions surrendered before the Lakers could get a shot. L.A. also finished nine of 34 from 3, their worst outing of the preseason.

Friday's preseason finale against Denver at Crypto.com Arena offers one more opportunity to improve that execution before the Lakers host Golden State in the regular-season opener.

articles.title: Bayern Munich youngster Lennart Karl needs to get back to what put him on the map
articles.summary: Lennart Karl needs to make some progress with FC Bayern.
articles.body:
Lennart Karl needs to wake up before "too much, too soon" becomes the story of his Bayern Munich career.

The talent is obvious, and the hype was understandable. But lately, Karl has looked like a player who has taken a step backward, and it is becoming increasingly difficult to ignore the flaws in his game.

The biggest issue is what happens when he does not have the ball. His off-the-ball movement needs to improve, because too often he looks content to wait for the game to come to him rather than actively trying to make things happen. At Bayern Munich, you cannot spend stretches of a match standing around and expect the ball to magically find you. You have to work for it, create passing lanes, attack space, and give your teammates options.

The painful part is that he was fantastic at edging his way in front of defenders or sneaking into open pockets of space last season. Now, his movement is, well, unmoving.

Then there is his predictable tendency to cut inside onto his left foot. Having a preferred move is not a problem; failing to execute it with enough pace is. Karl often seems determined to get onto his left, but takes too long doing it, allowing defenders to read the play, close the space, and turn a promising situation into another dead end. If the move is that predictable, he needs to be quicker, more direct, and willing to try something different.

There is a legitimate concern that Karl could become a victim of "too much, too soon." The attention, praise, and expectations have arrived at breakneck speed. Young players can start believing the hype before they have developed the consistency to justify it. Nobody should expect an 18-year-old to be the finished product, but potential cannot become an excuse for performances that lack urgency.

Bayern Munich fans only have so much patience, however. Supporters will forgive mistakes, inconsistency, and growing pains. What becomes harder to tolerate is a perceived lack of effort or tenacity. Karl could win plenty of people back simply by pressing harder, moving with more purpose, attacking defenders decisively, and showing that he is willing to fight for every minute.

There is also an important caveat — Karl suffered a serious thigh injury last summer, and it is entirely possible that he is still working his way back to full sharpness. That deserves consideration before anyone starts writing him off. He is still only 18, and a dip in form does not erase what he showed last season.

The point is not that Karl is suddenly a bad player. It is that he has to keep developing instead of relying on the reputation he built during his breakthrough campaign. The attention will not disappear, but he needs to learn to handle it while continuing to improve the less glamorous parts of his game.

The good news? There is still plenty of time to turn this around. Karl has the talent, the coaching, and the platform to get back on track. He just needs to show more urgency, more movement, and more fight. Sometimes, winning the fans back does not require a spectacular goal or a highlight-reel dribble. It starts with chasing a lost cause, making the extra run, and refusing to let a defender have an easy afternoon.

The hype can wait. The hard work cannot.

articles.title: Wrexham to batten down the hatches after defeat
articles.summary: Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson says criticism is inevitable after their home Championship defeat by West Bromwich Albion.
articles.body:
Phil Parkinson has challenged Wrexham to make an immediate response following their home defeat by West Bromwich Albion in the Championship.

Kieffer Moore's stunning 30-yard strike gave Wrexham the lead, but two goals in the final 11 minutes saw Albion hit back to win 2-1.

Wrexham are at the Racecourse again on Saturday when they face bottom of the table Preston North End.

Manager Parkinson said: "When you've lost a game at home it's time to batten down the hatches and come out strong as a group, and that's what we're going to do at the weekend.

"I'm sure we'll take criticism for the defeat, that's inevitable and we totally accept that.

"But there's a lot of resilience at that training ground and we're going to show it in the build-up to Preston."

West Brom hit back with late goals from Isaac Price and substitute Aune Heggebø to secure their first league win in four games.

The defeat denied Wrexham back-to-back home wins for the first time since February.

Parkinson said: "When you lose in that manner, it's obviously harder, isn't it? Because the lads could feel it, the game was there for us.

"No one's going to feel sorry for us in football. We've got to find a solution, look at the game and see which areas can we do better."

Parkinson praised striker Moore for his stunning goal, which put Wrexham ahead midway through the second half.

The Wales international was substituted soon after scoring, with Parkinson insisting the 34-year-old needed to be protected after playing the full game in Saturday's 1-1 draw at Derby County.

"Goals like that deserve to be part of a winning performance," Parkinson said.

"It was a brilliant goal and that's four he's got for the season, and he's got a few assists in there as well.

"He's had a really strong start to the season and he's scored all different types of goals as well.

"He played his first 90 for a while at the weekend and we went with him again, but also we've got to protect him to a certain degree."

articles.title: Incredible, Arsenal want struggling Liverpool star
articles.summary: Arsenal are reportedly in for one Liverpool star. The Gunners feel a deal is at least possible.Liverpool are currently dealing with a few difficult contract...
articles.body:
Arsenal are reportedly in for one Liverpool star. The Gunners feel a deal is at least possible.

Liverpool are currently dealing with a few difficult contract situations but they're situations that they've simply got to sort. Virgil van Dijk and Alisson Becker sit at the top of that list.

Both are genuine Liverpool legends and both, it has to be said, remain the most important and best options for their positions in the Reds' team. You can quite easily argue that they're just outright two of the best players in this team, in fact.

But they're out of contract next summer and also well into their 30s. Liverpool aren't known to hand out contracts to older players without a fight, as we saw two years ago with Mohamed Salah and Van Dijk.

So while those ones are up in the air, there's a contract at the other end of the scale that needs immediate attention.

Handing out big contracts to ageing players is something Liverpool don't like. But what about handing out big contracts to very young players?

That's the other situation at Anfield right now as they figure out what to do with Rio Ngumoha . Ngumoha has had a difficult start to the campaign after seeing Liverpool bizarrely sign two players in his natural position.

It means he's often been asked to play from the right - a role he isn't entirely suited to. This all comes as he's set to enter the final year of his contract next summer and wants a big pay rise to sign a new deal.

Teamtalk reports that Arsenal and Bayern Munich are keeping tabs on the situation. Both would love to sign Ngumoha and the teenager could, if he wanted, wait things out and join either of them for a small fee.

It would be particularly heartbreaking to see him at Arsenal, of course, and we imagine Liverpool will do all they can to sort this quickly. But that will almost certainly mean giving him more guarantees on the pitch.

That's difficult after spending nearly £200m on players in his position. Still, the Reds don't have much of a choice if they want to keep hold of one of England's brightest talents.

articles.title: Former Washington offensive coordinator talks Commanders' end-of-game gaffe vs Giants
articles.summary: What would one former Washington OC had told Jayden Daniels ahead of Sunday's final drive?
articles.body:
Former Washington offensive coordinator Scott Turner knows what it is like to be calling the plays for Washington late in games.

Turner, the son of former Washington Redskins head coach Norv Turner, served as Washington's offensive coordinator from 2020 to 2022 under former head coach Ron Rivera. What does Turner think about the final-minute disaster in which the Commanders failed to stop the clock before attempting a game-winning field goal?

Turner was a guest on the Grant & Danny Show Tuesday, and of course the target conversation was the horrible time management by the Commanders stealing away their opportunity to get the win. Grant Paulsen asked Turner, if the turnover just happened, what are you telling your quarterback now?

"You have to get yourself into field goal range, so at the point you discuss how many timeouts you have left, what are the plays that you are planning on calling and also what are the defenses you think you are going to be seeing," expressed Turner.

What would Turner have said at the time when the Commanders reached the 26-yard line on a completion to Treylon Burks, and he was able to get out of bounds? "At that point I would say, 'Hey, we are in field goal range, and we don't have any timeouts."

The Commanders then ran Rachaad White to the 24-yard line. "I understand they wanted to get closer. They missed an extra point early in the game. The weather was an issue. The closer you get, the higher the percentage you have of making the kick."

What does Turner think, in hindsight, about what he saw in the Commanders' actions on the final play? "It didn't look like there was a plan. Everything should be quiet (in the OC headset) in that situation." Turner then briefly described a time when he was calling plays for the Raiders. Several people started talking to him at once, and he got distracted.

Turner then reiterated, "There's only 40 seconds left on the clock. You want to get that play call into the quarterback, so he can call the play in the huddle, and you can then get to the line."

Turner reiterated that in the pressure-packed last minute, you don't want to be coming up with your plan. You want to have a plan already prepared and discussed with your quarterback. Instead, you want to focus on executing your plan.

Perhaps that's the lesson for first-year offensive coordinator David Blough. Then again, we don't know what Jayden Daniels was told to do on that last play, do we?

Here is a look at the list of current unrestricted free agents sorted by the amount of snaps they have played so far this season:

This chart shows the ages of the draft class at the time of the draft. Greens signifies the age of 66% of the prospects they have drafted in this range, yellow 33% and red is an age they have never taken in this range. So while it is unlikely they select a red player, it isn't impossible.

OBR VIP's can see my full October draft board with each position on it here .

The room starts with Harold Fannin who last year joined the top ten for the most receiving yards ny a rookie tight end in NFL history. The eight players ahead of him were selected in the top 15 picks other than Sam Laporta at 34. Making Fannin a massive steal at pick 67. Last year he was producing 46 yards per game on average, this has dropped to 31 in 2026. Partly due to more mouths to feed in the offense and also taking some time to get going but there is no reason he won't return to higher numbers late in the season and next year.

The big issue is his run blocking. While improved pass blocking would be beneficial, the amount of staying in to block that the modern tight end does now is minimal. What the Cleveland Browns really need to get to, is not having to take him out the game on run plays or leave him in there as a blocking liability. What he does in the blocking game will dictate if he is just a pumped up receiver like Kyle Pitts or if he can slightly improve his blocking then he can join a tier with someone like Trey McBride.

To this end they need to go out and aggressively target another tight end in free agency. Someone that can be a net positive in the blocking game. You ideally don't want to go out and get a one dimensional player either. Else it is clear to the defense whether it is a run or a pass based on which tight end is out there. This isn't a role they can leave to the draft like they tried to do this season. You don't know where players are going to get selected and it isn't a position you regularly see instant impact from outside the first round.

When it comes to the third tight end, they should be considering all options. The first two names to look at will be Joe Royer and Carsen Ryan, see if you have anything in either player come the end of the season. At the same time being back Blake Whiteheart to keep battling for a roster spot as he is a serviceable third tight end. Then also don't rule out selecting someone else too, it is a shame Terrance Carter is such an old prospect but maybe a later day three pick. Having three of four players battling for the depth of the roster is valuable. It also means if multiple impress you can potentially carry four next season rather than a special teams fullback as many teams are leaning into the tight end position more and more.

articles.title: Jaguars’ Parker Washington earns Steve Smith comp from Marcus Spears
articles.summary: Parker Washington has quickly become one of Trevor Lawrence’s most trusted weapons for the Jacksonville Jaguars, and his latest performance has him drawing...
articles.body:
Parker Washington has quickly become one of Trevor Lawrence's most trusted weapons for the Jacksonville Jaguars , and his latest performance has him drawing comparisons to one of the toughest receivers of his generation.

Washington was the star of Jacksonville's 19-17 win over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday at Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London. He caught six passes for 124 yards and accounted for both of the Jaguars' touchdowns, starting with a 51-yard catch-and-run in the first quarter.

His second score was the one that got everyone talking. Facing fourth-and-5 with 3:20 remaining, Lawrence fired a 27-yard pass to Washington, who hauled it in with one hand over cornerback Riq Woolen to give Jacksonville a 16-14 lead.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

On ESPN's "NFL Live," Mina Kimes and the crew broke down the play , with Kimes praising the aggressiveness that head coach Liam Coen has instilled in his quarterback since arriving last season.

"I love that he still trusted Parker Washington enough to throw it downfield for that incredible catch," Kimes said.

Marcus Spears pointed out that Washington's frame is not the typical build for contested catches, which made Lawrence's willingness to give him a chance even more telling.

"Your size doesn't lend itself to 50-50 balls, and Trevor just throws that mug anyway," Spears said. "He's so tough. Steve Smith, to me."

The comparison to the former Carolina Panthers star, a five-time Pro Bowler known for his stocky frame and fearless style, was quickly seconded.

"I literally was just about to say Steve," came the reply on set. "Not as much of an edge, but just that stocky body."

Washington has been building toward this kind of breakout. Through five games, he has 22 catches for 352 yards and four touchdowns, establishing himself as Lawrence's top downfield option.

His big day also helped keep Jacksonville rolling. Cam Little drilled a 57-yard field goal as time expired to win it , improving the Jaguars to 4-1 and keeping them atop the AFC South. Jacksonville is now 12-1 over its last 13 games, according to ESPN.

The Jaguars will stay in London for Week 6, where they will face the Houston Texans in a key division matchup .

articles.title: What Tommy Lloyd, Motiejus Krivas and Derek Dixon said after Arizona’s exhibition win over San Francisco
articles.summary: Arizona men’s basketball started preseason play in dominating fashion with a 93-69 win over San Francisco. Center Motiejus Krivas led the Wildcats with 20 po...
articles.body:
Arizona men's basketball started preseason play in dominating fashion with a 93-69 win over San Francisco. Center Motiejus Krivas led the Wildcats with 20 points while forward Ivan Kharchenkov added in 18 of his own.

Freshman Caleb Holt and North Carolina transfer Derek Dixon also had double-digit scoring performances and Arizona forced 19 turnovers. UA plays its second exhibition on Friday against San Diego State.

Our game recap can be found here . Below is what head coach Tommy Lloyd , Krivas and Dixon had to say following the win over San Francisco:

Lloyd on the win : "It was a great experience, and you try not to get too caught up in the minutia. I mean, we just needed reps. We needed reps against somebody else, and to get some live bullets out there and kind of see how guys kind of play and kind of spontaneous situations. I think it's great. I'm excited to break down the film. I'm sure there's a lot of really good things, and I'm sure there's a lot of other things we can learn from as well."

On what stood out and what could be improved : "I don't know. The foreign tour was a great experience, but I don't know if there's a direct correlation between taking a foreign tour and where your team is right now. It's just an amazing thing. It's year 28 for me in college basketball at this level, and I'm just always amazed how you have to start over every single time. Even when you come back from a foreign trip, you feel like, 'oh no, you have to start over.' It's just how it works, and so you better lock into that beginner's mindset and fall in love with the process and the work, otherwise you're going to get sloppy and skip steps. So I'm trying to hold myself accountable to be there for these guys and coach them where they're at, not be frustrated by where you might hope they would be, and experiences like this are amazing catalysts to see what we can do with it and how much better we can be."

On managing fan reactions to exhibitions : "Well, first off, you don't get sidetracked by how your fan base might feel. You got to lock into the process, like I said earlier, and you got to help the guys understand what it takes to win, and so that's what we've really been focused on. I have inklings in my mind of what I'm going to see when I watch the film, but I kind of want to watch the film before I come out and say thoughts that may not be entirely true."

On Caleb Holt's performance : "Well, Caleb's really motivated to be a great all-around player and to really understand the nuances of the game, and so he's shouldered a heavy burden on his own of trying to learn. So, you're talking about a guy that has just kind of risen through the ranks at the highest levels of kind of high school basketball and international basketball just with his effort and his kind of raw instincts and so now he's trying to kind of refine himself a little bit. This guy works incredibly hard and he's really a skilled player, and he's a unique player. So, I'm just excited to kind of help him on the journey, and then just make sure that I'm trying to teach it, but I definitely don't want to put the shackles on this guy or make him a robot, because I think he's a guy that has to kind of be turned loose a little bit. Yeah, there's probably going to be a few head scratching plays, but there might also be some head scratching plays in a positive direction as well."

On JJ Mandaquit's performance : "He was great. JJ has really made a lot of progress in the last month. He really did start practicing for us consistently till about the last month, and I thought he looked great out there and I think as he gets a little bit more comfortable, we get a little bit more comfortable with him, his teammates get more comfortable. I think he's going to be a guy that really really impacts winning."

On if there is any emphasis of physical safety given the game doesn't go on record : "We don't talk specifically about it. We're trying not to run the guys into the ground, but you got to take a few minutes and kind of push them a little bit to see where they're at physically and see if they can fight through some fatigue thresholds and things like that. Then the game is the game. We don't want to be reckless, but you got to play. You got to play. You got to get on the floor. There's going to be contact. So, you know, if you shy away from that, I don't know if you're going to give yourself a real look. So, no, I know there were some guys on the floor today, and maybe a couple more opportunities we could have gotten on the floor. That's something we take a lot of pride in."

On the team's physicality : "We got a high standard for that. I'm sure there were moments we were, and I'm sure there's going to be moments I watch that we're going to be able to ask for more with that stuff. We always want to play a physical brand of basketball. I think that's the most fun way to play and the most effective way to play."

On Krivas' defensive presence : "I mean, honestly, I think I have a crazy high standard for Mo. I thought defensively he was just okay tonight. You know what I mean? I don't think he was as good in some of those downhill situations. Usually, he's elite in those. Their guard, the Argentinian kid, played with a bunch of swag and aggression, and had a little bit of success down there. He gets a lot of credit for that, but our guards are part of that equation too. If the ball screen coverage that we got Mo in, you're going to give up some penetration. Usually, you're giving up penetration, and you're able to kind of guard the three-point line a little bit better with it, and you're relying on them to play oversides at the rim, but your guard's got to be part of that downhill, and whether that's breaking on a dump down pass to the big, if it's choking down on when the guard shoots a floater and Mo can test it, so we got to really go look at it and figure out if they were just one-offs or if there's some themes that we gotta do. You're right in the sense that Mo is a really important part of our defense and he's super impactful there. I know he had some possessions where he did alter shots and I love having Mo on the court defensively for sure."

On the rotation : "We're figuring that all out. There's been a lot of moving parts, so it's just kind of figuring out what's going to put the pieces in the right place, and what you think might be that answer today might not be the answer in three weeks from now. So just keeping an open mind and trying a few things, and then kind of evaluating them and then making decisions moving forward."

On forcing 19 turnovers : "Hopefully we can turn teams over. We really didn't let loose a lot defensively tonight. I mean, they ended up in a lot of downhill penetration, and that's high risk basketball. You had to guard small areas against big guys, and those passes could get tough. So maybe we got a few turnovers on that, and then our running game got going a little bit finally towards the second half of that second half when we were able to make a little bit of a run and give ourselves a little bit of a margin."

On taking care of the ball : "They did a great job taking care of the ball overall. I don't know if it's going to be realistic to have eight turnovers every game the way we want to play, but today they did a good job of it. Let's hope that trend continues."

On Ivan Kharchenkov's high motor and energy : "Ivan's super talented, and he's super impactful in all facets of the game. The biggest thing I have for Ivan is just staying steady, staying physical, staying on balance. He doesn't need to do tricky things to impact the game, and just making sure he stays the course when he's making those types of decisions. So, I mean, Ivan is a key part of what we did, especially in the second half of last year, and obviously it looks like he's going to need to even expand on that role this year."

On Mandaquit and Dixon being on the court together : "Going back a lot of years, I've always liked having two point guard types on the floor. I think that's can be a great way to play if you have a group of guys and it makes sense. So I just think it allows JJ, I mean first off it allows Derek to to get some extended run and it allows JJ to kind of get the minutes he needs to get. Those two guys complement each other and obviously I think Derek's a really good point guard who's had a really good summer and fall for us. When you put him alongside JJ, maybe he can get off the ball a little bit because he's also a dynamic shooter."

On Bryce James starting : "I didn't want to overthink it. Bryce has had a good fall for us and continues to grow as a player, and I think starting Bryce, I just felt like kind of maybe puts the rotation in the right way and maybe have some good impactful guys coming off the bench. I just kind of wanted to see how that looked and felt today. I don't know what I'm going to do Friday, and we'll talk to the staff tomorrow about what we think is best. I'm not going to overthink that one, it's just the first few minutes of a 40-minute game."

On handling RJ Godfrey's eligibility situation : "I make decisions with what I have at hand. RJ couldn't play today, so there was no thought of anything."

On having with/without Godfrey plans : "Even if RJ was eligible, I would have a with or without plan. I mean, because he's not going to play 40 minutes. We've been working on plans, kind of what we want to do when RJ's on the court. We spend a lot of time on that. We spend a lot of time on what we're going to do when RJ is off the court. So, it's kind of how we have to build our team. Just based on the different style and different types of personnel we have. I'm going to focus and lean towards the side where I know the guys that can play. I mean, that's the only common sense thing to do."

On the status of Evan Otten and Endurance Aiyamenkhue : "Evan is fine. He hopefully, maybe next game, he can get a little bit more run. He's done a good job and is starting to make progress. Indy. Endi, I think he's out for a bit, but I don't think much longer. I don't have an exact timeline."

On how the San Diego State exhibition came to be : "Guys on our staff have a good relationship with some guys in their staff, and we have a lot of respect for their program. Obviously, we wanted to play what we felt was going to be like a really challenging game. So we ask them, and they agree. I mean, it wasn't much more than that. If you're asking me anything about their team other than how good they have been, I really don't have any idea. Every team is so new right now, but I'm assuming they got great DNA and they got winning DNA because that's what that program's been about."

On if it's odd that San Diego State is part of the newly formed Pac-12 : "Where do we want to start with odd? Everything's odd right now. I'm sure it's gonna be a good basketball conference and with the Pac-12, kind of the old Pac-12, we were part of dissolving. I think the West Coast needs a strong basketball conference once again. So hopefully, this new Pac-12 can really provide that."

Dixon on playing in McKale for the first time : "I felt really good. I'm lucky to play with a lot of really good players, so they make it easy for me. It felt good to come out here and play against somebody else for the first time. I thought the fans were pretty good tonight, and hopefully, we can get them the same way Friday, maybe a little more."

On if he is a downhill type of player : "I think I try to mix it up. When the driving lanes are there for me, take them and just try to make plays for my teammates when I can. I try to pride myself on being a three-level scorer, being able to get downhill, make plays for others, get to the mid-range, stop and pop if I need it, and then obviously my shooting is something that I can always fall back on."

On playing with Mandaquit : "I think it's just different. You have somebody else who's initiating and creating, so I can try and be a little bit more aggressive coming off screens, coming off actions."

On having a big backcourt : "I think we've got size, like you said, at all positions, which is going to help us really defensively. I thought we could have been better on the boards tonight, which is something we'll continue to work on, especially with our size being better on the boards."

On if he feels the team is further along in its development : "I think we've had a really good couple months of preseason since we've been back, just building up what we're trying to do and how we're trying to play. So I definitely felt a little bit better out there. I think the ball moved a little bit better, and yeah, just excited to keep growing."

Krivas on getting the ball more inside this year : "You probably can see that the ball is like going a little bit more in the paint, and that's credit to these guys. I don't know. We just try to play good team basketball and involve everyone and get these shots. Nobody is holding the ball too long."

On if his conditioning is there to play more minutes : "If I can, I will. Maybe not yet, but it will be."

On having a big backcourt : "I feel like in the first half we didn't do a good job on defense. We let their guards get kind of comfortable, but in the second half I feel like we did better jumping. As Derek said, we have to get those balls."

On defending better in downhill situations : "Just like in the drop coverage, kind of play with them, like make them think what to do. Like, 'Can I shoot?' Then they see me, like 'Can I pass?' So make them make a decision and impact the ball as much as I can."

On Kharchenkov's energy plays : "It's huge. It's probably the best play to hype the crowd and the team, and it just shows that guys play with huge effort and makes the team follow."

On what he remembers about playing San Diego State last season : "I remember it was a really hard game. We couldn't make threes like that's how they play. They just make you shoot tough shots and they're a really physical team, really great program. So yeah, we have to clean up those areas of playing physically from the start."

articles.title: Bills DC Jim Leonhard makes strong declaration on fixing Buffalo’s putrid defense
articles.summary: Buffalo Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said Tuesday that he is evaluating every decision he makes after another high-scoring game exposed the unit’...
articles.body:
Buffalo Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard said Tuesday that he is evaluating every decision he makes after another high-scoring game exposed the unit's inconsistency.

The Bills improved to 4-1 with Monday's 37-34 overtime victory over the Los Angeles Rams at SoFi Stadium, but Buffalo has allowed at least 30 points in three of its first five games.

Through Week 5, the Bills have surrendered 141 points, averaging 28.2 per game and ranking 28th in the NFL. Their offense has averaged 32.8 points, helping Buffalo remain atop the AFC East despite the defensive struggles. The unit has also struggled to limit opponents' total yardage and passing production.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

The Buffalo News' Lance Lysowski took to X, formerly Twitter, to share the defensive coordinator's assessment, which began with scrutiny of his own decisions.

"It's too inconsistent to pretend that we're building and working and making improvements. Everything's being evaluated right now. Starting with every decision I'm making."

The Rams gained 454 total yards Monday as Matthew Stafford threw for 383 yards and three touchdowns. Puka Nacua caught a career-high 17 passes for 138 yards and a touchdown.

The Bills also allowed the Rams to drive for a tying score in the final seconds of regulation. Kyren Williams punched it in from the 1-yard line with five seconds remaining, sending the game to overtime.

Buffalo produced a critical overtime play when Greg Rousseau blocked Harrison Mevis' potential game-winning field goal. Tyler Bass later secured the victory with a 45-yard kick.

Leonhard is in his first season as Buffalo's defensive coordinator after serving as the Denver Broncos' defensive pass game coordinator. He has installed an aggressive, attacking scheme built around a 3-4 base.

The coordinator has previously raised concerns about inconsistent results, and Tuesday's remarks rejected the suggestion that the unit is steadily improving. He did not identify specific personnel changes in the quoted comments.

articles.title: Christian Horner on F1 absence: ‘This is why people will now see a different side to me’
articles.summary: EXCLUSIVE INTERVIEW: Exclusive: After a tumultuous conclusion to his time at Red Bull, Horner is enjoying life in the slow lane. But he’s not done yet. Kiera...
articles.body:
For Christian Horner , after 14 world championships, two decades and one frenzied ride in Formula 1 , it has been an unprecedented period of serenity.

"I did 405 races in succession," he tells me straight off the bat, dialling in on a video call with The Independent from his home in Highgate, North London. "This is really the first time in 35 years that I haven't been on that hamster wheel."

And it's the simple things away from the "brutal" schedule of top-tier motorsport – your parents' evenings, your kids' sports matches, life in the slow lane – which the 52-year-old is not only embracing but relishing. "Whether it was walking my son to school this morning, when I would normally have been in Singapore, or not missing my daughter's birthday tomorrow, which I obviously would have done before, it's those little things that you appreciate," he says.

"And I think they appreciate them, too".

It has been 15 months since Formula 1's ultimate love-him or loathe-him figure, who took charge and developed Red Bull Racing from the "fizzy drinks team" into the modern-day F1 juggernaut, was unceremoniously booted out as team boss . A job he loved, savoured and is yet to receive a specific reason for losing.

We speak off the back of the one-off race in Malaysia at the start of October, when Max Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first victory as an engine supplier. That project, in partnership with Ford, was ambitiously launched by Horner, who admitted a sense of pride upon seeing his old colleagues bask in victory once more.

"Very few people can understand the scale of that challenge," he says. "For a group of people within five years to have taken on the best in the industry and won a grand prix on their 16th start is outstanding. I had some wonderful messages from within the team – it was very gratifying."

A career high point, a year on from the tumultuous final 18 months in charge of Red Bull. "The higher you rise, the sharper the knives," his wife, Spice Girl pop star Geri Halliwell , told him amid a period shrouded in turmoil off the track , in contrast to triumph on the racing line. After allegations of controlling and coercive behaviour levelled at him at the start of 2024 from a female colleague, which Horner always denied and which were twice dismissed by independent lawyers, the man himself is now having his say in his new book, Drive .

"What doesn't break you makes you stronger," he says, matter-of-factly, looking back on a chapter which saw him dominate the front pages more than the back. "It was a difficult period. In life, there are always going to be challenges and you're always learning. Now for me, it's about asking what comes next."

Seldom has Horner opened up and been so frank about his final few years at the Red Bull helm. From his lawyer asking "are you sat down?" when the initial allegation was made, to the "strange feeling" at the back end of his time as team boss – with those knives sharpening to breaking point – Horner gets as much off his chest and onto paper as realistically viable.

But throughout it all, one constant theme is palpable throughout the 320 pages: the unwavering support from his wife, Geri.

"She was phenomenal," he acknowledges. "As your wife, as your partner and as your friend, she showed incredible support and strength. Of course, it's always your partner that you offload your bad days, as well as your good days. She's been an absolute pillar of strength and has always been quick to offer perspective."

Beyond the scandal, there is heaps of insight and anecdotes to absorb. Horner speaks candidly about his failed attempt at making it as a driver and the moment Juan Pablo Montoya's aggressive line into a corner in Estoril made him realise he was not cut from the same cloth. He retired, aged 25. At that juncture, plenty would have set their sights away from motorsport. Plenty do. Not Horner.

Taking charge of Arden Motorsport, he experienced waves of success in Formula 3000. Then, encouraged by Bernie Ecclestone , he joined forces with Red Bull's otherworldly attempt to get into motorsport. In 2005, he became the sport's youngest-ever team principal at the age of 31.

"I never felt I was out of my depth" he recalls. "I just broke things down and approached them in the way I always had: finding sensible solutions to whatever problems there were.

"The scale of Formula One was different from anything I'd experienced previously, but the problems were all very much the same. F1 is a people business, sharing a common goal and vision and working as a team."

Persuading design guru Adrian Newey to join Red Bull in year one (Horner speaks in fascinating depth in the book about Newey's exit from the team, 20 years later) was the catalyst for the success that followed. Eight drivers' championships – four with Sebastian Vettel, four with Max Verstappen – and six constructors' titles make Horner one of the most successful team principals of his generation. He is one short of arch rival Toto Wolff's tally of 15 titles.

His first of each era, 2010 with Vettel and that infamous 2021 finale with Verstappen, are the ones that stand out. "I think of 2009, too, because it was the first year we were really competitive," he says, recalling Jenson Button limping to the title with Brawn. "If that season had gone on longer, we would have won.

"But 2010 was so special because it was the realisation of actually having a world champion. Then obviously 2021, after all of Mercedes' dominant years, you couldn't have scripted what happened there. It was insane and an incredible sense of achievement."

A constant confidante throughout it all was F1's former kingmaker Ecclestone: godfather to Horner's daughter, Olivia. Horner was also best man at Ecclestone's wedding to current wife Fabiana. A friendship built on trust, sprinkled with a bit of old-school joshing.

"Bernie would often drop things into conversations to diffuse the tension," Horner says. "He was very good at coming up to you just before a grand prix and telling you: 'Don't scew it up!'

"That was probably not the advice you needed at that moment in time, but it created a bit of levity. He had a way of doing that, and it was always very Bernie."

The pair now both have a watching brief. Horner, who received a £67m payout from Red Bull, admits he still tunes in for most qualifying sessions and race-days, albeit as he joins the chorus of dissenters of this year's "overly complex" set of regulations. His only return to the paddock since leaving the sport came at Silverstone this year, where he was mobbed from all quarters.

Inevitably, speculation about his next move is a constant topic of discussion. Waves were made a few weeks back when Horner declared Ferrari was "the dream" job and the only organisation he'd join without a stake in the team – a condition he has previously publicised.

"It was all taken out of context because I was trying to be respectful to the Ferrari brand because they are different to other teams," he says now. Less a backtrack, more a frank assessment. "It's the longest-standing team and the most prominent team in Formula One and they're not going to sell equity in it.

"It coincided with comments from drivers internally and then you put two and two together and come up with eight. From my perspective, there's 11 teams in Formula One. There's potentially a 12th entry." Hint hint. "But I'm not in a rush to do anything."

Be that as it may, could Horner really be content with not running a Formula 1 team ever again? As well as Ferrari, he has been closely linked with Alpine and Aston Martin. "Look, I've had a great run in the sport, I've got a healthy win ratio," he says. Indeed, the back of his book reads: 405 races, 287 podiums, 124 grand prix victories, 14 world championships.

"It would have to be for the right project. I still love the sport. I enjoy the competition. I love working with people, but it would need to be the right team. Otherwise, I'm content doing what I'm doing at the moment."

Current undertakings include consultancy work for Oakley Capital, now the major shareholder for Ben Ainslie's GB1 America's Cup team. He has also attended MotoGP this year and, alongside Geri, owns eight racehorses.

But most pertinent is his role as the present father to 13-year-old daughter Olivia, nine-year-old son Monty and step-daughter Bluebell, 20. None of whom, to Horner's paternal relief, want to follow their dad into motorsport. He actually says in the book that he is now "very aware of his own mortality", a nod to the tragic loss of his former partner Beverley Allen, mother to Olivia, last year from eye cancer at the age of 58.

"It must be enormously difficult as a parent watching your child racing and particularly at levels like Formula 1," he says. "It's one of those sports with true jeopardy. I would only encourage them to follow their dreams. Being Formula One drivers doesn't seem to appeal to them."

And what does Horner want readers of his new memoir to take away from his own topsy-turvy experience? "There's the ups and the downs and all the challenges that life throws at you," he signs off. "But you brush yourself down, you pick yourself up, and you go again.

"I hope people see a different side to me than what is portrayed, particularly through some of the documentaries that exist! I've tried to lift the lid on the real person behind the team uniform."

articles.title: España da un golpe sobre la mesa ante Portugal y acaricia el liderato de grupo
articles.standfirst: España derrota a la vigente campeona de Europa por 2-4
articles.summary: España derrota a la vigente campeona de Europa por 2-4
articles.body: La selección española de hockey sobre patines dio este martes un golpe de autoridad al derrotar a la vigente campeona de Europa, Portugal (2-4), a la que desarboló con 26 minutos iniciales sobresalientes para dejar prácticamente encarrilado el liderato del Grupo A del Mundial que se disputa en Asunción (Paraguay). El combinado que dirige Pere Varias firmó un estreno inmejorable en el campeonato. Si el lunes se impuso a Italia (3-2), la selección que la apartó de las medallas en el último Europeo, este martes hizo lo propio ante Portugal, verdugo de España en las semifinales de aquella misma cita continental. Si ante los transalpinos el factor diferencial fue el capitán Pau Bargalló, autor de un triplete, frente al conjunto luso brilló el bloque español. Una actuación coral sobresaliente, especialmente en la primera mitad y el arranque de la segunda, permitió a España desarbolar a su rival y plasmar su superioridad con los tantos de Eloi Cervera, Nil Roca y Marc Grau. Con el encuentro encarrilado, España rebajó la intensidad y la concentración, una circunstancia que Portugal aprovechó para aferrarse al partido. El orgullo y la calidad individual del conjunto luso reactivaron una contienda que parecía sentenciada cuando Miguel Rocha sorprendió con un lanzamiento lejano para establecer el 1-3 a diez minutos del final (min. 40). El partido entró entonces en una fase de máxima tensión, acentuada por una tarjeta azul a Marc Grau que dejó a España en inferioridad numérica. Portugal no desaprovechó la ventaja y Gonçalo Alves volvió a batir la portería española con otro lanzamiento lejano para situar el 2-3 (min.49). Lo que había sido una exhibición española se convirtió en un ejercicio de resistencia. Como ya sucediera ante Italia, cuando supo reaccionar en los momentos de mayor presión, el equipo de Varias tuvo que recurrir a su capacidad de sufrimiento para proteger una victoria de enorme valor. Portugal apostó incluso por el portero-jugador en el último minuto, pero España resistió el asedio y, en el último segundo, Pol Manrubia aprovechó que la portería lusa estaba vacía para firmar el definitivo 2-4. España afrontará este miércoles (20:30 hora española) el último compromiso de la fase de grupos ante Suiza, un encuentro en el que buscará certificar matemáticamente la primera plaza y conocer a su rival en los cuartos de final. 2 - Portugal: Henriques; Miranda, Bessa, Rodrigues, Ramos, -cinco inicial-, Querido, Rocha (1), Alves (1), Nunes y Edo (p.s). 4 - España: Ballart; Bargalló, Grau (1), Nil Roca (1), Cervera (1), -cinco inicial-, Llanes, Carballeira, Manrubia (1), Morales y Blai Roca (p.s). Goles: 0-1, min.7: Eloi Cervera. 0-2, min.8: Nil Roca. 0-3, min.26: Marc Grau. 1-3, min.40: Miguel Rocha. 2-3, min.49: Gonçalo Alves. 2-4, min.49: Pol Manrubia. Árbitros: Luca Molli (ITA) y Anthony Hyde (USA). Por parte de Portugal, mostraron tarjeta amarilla a Rafael Bessa (min. 19), al técnico José Pinto (min. 24) y a Luis Querido (min. 41). Por parte de España, amonestaron con tarjeta amarilla a Nil Roca (min. 1), Biel Llanes y Pau Bargalló (ambos en el min. 42). Además, mostraron tarjeta azul a Marc Grau (min. 48). articles.title: NHL Power Rankings See Hurricanes and Oilers Vault to Top Spots
articles.summary: They sure grow up fast, don't they?
articles.body:
Hockey fans spent months longing for the NHL season to start, and now the early-season storylines are taking shape.

The B/R hockey staff is in midseason form after cranking out another installment of Power Rankings heading toward the third full week of the 2026-27 schedule.

Take a look at what we came up with and drop a thought in the app comments.

Statistics through games of Monday, Oct. 12.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | Utah Mammoth | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

The Flames started 0-5-0 for the first time in franchise history, scoring just eight goals along the way, but coach Ryan Huska preached patience. "We've slowly been getting better, and that's the most important thing," he said .

It paid off on Tuesday, with a win against Anaheim.

A 3-2 shootout loss to Seattle at home made it eight straight games in which the Flyers were held to two or fewer goals. Philadelphia was 21st in the league with 240 goals in 2025-26. The record for fewest goals in an 84-game season is 201, in 1993-94.

The Blackhawks won at Carolina on Saturday and continued a turnaround after a 0-3-0 road start in which they were outscored 15-5. "I have no idea when it's going to be, but this group's going to win," coach Jeff Blashill said , "100 percent."

New captain Connor Bedard returned on Tuesday, leading Chicago to a home win over the Penguins.

Overreactions to the Start of the Season

Early optimism evolved into familiar pessimism for the Canucks, who began the season with two wins in three games before losing four straight, in which they were outscored 20-7. They'll return home from a six-game road trip on Oct. 20.

It's already been a tough start for the Kings, and it didn't help when forwards Mats Zuccarello and Alex Turcotte were placed on injured reserve. "We're competitors in here. We hate losing, and we want to win," goalie Darcy Kuemper said .

Coach Todd McLellan is taking a collective leadership tack for the Red Wings, amid the ongoing turmoil surrounding ex-captain Dylan Larkin. "There's a lot of different people in different leadership roles on our team right now," he said .

Depth of skill hadn't translated into goals for the Devils in 2026-27. New Jersey scored three or fewer goals in three of its first five games, including a shutout by the New York Islanders and one goal in a home loss to Ottawa.

That changed on Tuesday, as they tallied five in an overtime win over the Red Wings.

A home loss to streaking Tampa Bay wasn't ideal, but it gave coach Pete DeBoer a better idea of where his team stands. "It was a good measuring stick game for us," he said . "We passed quite a few of the tests in my mind of how we have to play."

The Isles responded on Tuesday with a home win against Vancouver.

The Blue Jackets went to a shootout to defeat Pittsburgh, then led 2-0 in St. Louis a day later before the tanks ran dry in a 5-3 loss. "The thought process got away from us," coach Rick Bowness said , "and the intensity necessary left us."

It didn't get any better on Tuesday after getting crushed at home by Florida.

It didn't sound super serious at the outset, but it's never good news when one of your best players, in this case defenseman Rasmus Dahlin, leaves a game and doesn't accompany the team on a road trip. "Day to day," coach Lindy Ruff said .

The Blues skidded in Colorado and Chicago, losing 6-1 and 4-2, but rebounded in a raucous home win against Columbus. "Our fans support every single home game ... these past three days they've been absolutely humming," Jimmy Snuggerud said .

They took those good vibes on the road and demolished the Senators in Ottawa on Tuesday.

An iffy start for Jakub Dobes (1-1-1, .857 save percentage) opened the door for AHL call-up Jacob Fowler, who stopped 30 shots to blank Detroit on Saturday. He is the fifth Montreal goalie to have multiple NHL shutouts at age 21 or younger.

It took him until game six, but Brady Tkachuk finally got a point in a Panthers sweater when he assisted on Sam Reinhart's goal in the second period of a Monday loss at Buffalo. He had seven hits and three shots in 16:32 of ice time.

The younger Tkachuk took that as a springboard for a monster game on Tuesday, recording a hat trick versus the Blue Jackets.

The Stars scored 11 goals in their first five games, and just one on the power play, and it won't help that forward Matt Duchene is now expected to miss three months after surgery to repair a core injury that he dealt with in training camp.

The Predators frittered away a lead, gave up a late goal, and lost in a shootout to Ottawa. "It's been a little common in the past few games," forward Jonathan Marchessault said . "We kind of lay off the gas a little bit and let teams back in."

Darnell Nurse played 798 games for Edmonton, but he'd never played in the Oilers' rink as a visitor until Saturday's 3-1 loss. "It was odd. Never been through that before, but preparation is no different," he said . "Just go out there and play."

Ending a three-game slide (0-2-1) with a shootout win against a tough Dallas team after allowing a late tying goal provided a significant moment for coach Dan Muse. "This was way better," he said . "For me, it's an exciting step for us to take."

Pittsburgh took a step back Tuesday in Chicago, though, despite a Sidney Crosby goal.

Take a breath, Toronto fans. Gavin McKenna might be ready for the NHL after all. The top overall pick was pointless in his first three games but had a goal and three assists in his next three. "Every game he is taking steps," coach Jim Hiller said .

He scored Tuesday night against the Mammoth, but the Leafs lost in Utah.

Alex Ovechkin scored on his 190th goalie when he beat the Kraken's Joey Daccord, but the Capitals saw a brief two-game win streak halted by Seattle. Washington won three of its first four games in which it scored at least three goals.

A Saturday loss to Toronto was just the second of the season, and the first at home for Colorado, but coach Jared Bednar was not having it. "You got the team doing it right," he said , "and you got a couple of guys that weren't there for us (Saturday)."

The Bruins finished their six-game early-season purgatory without defenseman Charlie McAvoy, who was suspended for a slash on Buffalo forward Zach Benson in the playoffs. Boston was held to one goal twice, but scored 18 in the other four.

Just when it seemed the Jets had started well enough to deflect the Connor Hellebuyck drama, it's back. NHL Insider David Pagnotta suggested the goalie could return to the team if a long-discussed trade doesn't happen soon.

Listing the league's premier goal-scorers? It'll probably be a while before you get to Nick Schmaltz. Still, the 30-year-old did score 33 times last season and had six goals in four of Utah's first games in 2026-27, setting a pace for 67 in 84 games.

Break up the Kraken! Seattle had six goals dumped on it by Vegas in an Oct. 6 home loss but took to the road for a five-game trip that opened with 11 goals scored in consecutive games at Detroit (6-3) and Washington (5-3).

The Kraken followed that up with another win, a shootout victory over the hapless Flyers on Tuesday.

It was bad enough when Igor Shesterkin left Friday's game . It got far worse when it was announced that he was done for the season —leaving the New York net (thanks to a lingering injury to backup Joonas Korpisalo) to 24-year-old Dylan Garand, who entered 2026-27 having made three career starts.

The Ducks' 4-2 win at Calgary lifted them to 4-1-0 for the fifth time in franchise history, following similar starts in 2011-12, 2013-14, 2014-15, and 2019-20. Anaheim started 3-0-2 on the way to the franchise's lone Stanley Cup in 2006-07.

Quinn Hughes proved his worth to the Wild with points in six straight games to open the season, the sixth-longest season-opening streak in league history by an American-born defenseman. He had 76 points in 2025-26.

The Golden Knights split their first two games of the season but had reeled off four straight wins (and allowed just eight goals) before the early streak ended when they lost 4-2 on Monday at Minnesota. Jack Eichel has 12 points in six games.

There's championship muscle memory in the Tampa Bay locker room, but early success helps indoctrinate the new guys, too. "You want to be able to build some confidence within the team," forward Brandon Hagel said , "within the group."

It wasn't a reach to suggest Linus Ullmark's play would be a key factor for the Tkachuk-less Senators this season and the 33-year-old Swede responded with a great start, winning his first five appearances while allowing just six goals.

Having the league's top scorers in northern Alberta isn't a novelty, but raise your hand if you had the Oilers, under Mike Babcock, as the last team in the NHL without a regulation loss. Edmonton was 2-2-1 through five games last season.

Reigning Conn Smythe Trophy winner Jordan Staal will miss at least a month as the Hurricanes chase a repeat after tearing a calf during warmups for a Sunday game in Philadelphia. Staal had 12 points in 19 playoff games in Carolina's cup run.

articles.title: Predicting WWE Survivor Series 2026 Men's, Women's War Games Participants
articles.summary: The annual Thanksgiving week tradition returns on Saturday, November 28 from Houston's Daikin Park as WWE presents Survivor Series: War Games.
articles.body:
The annual Thanksgiving week tradition returns on Saturday, November 28 from Houston's Daikin Park as WWE presents Survivor Series: War Games.

The men's and women's War Games matches will be at the center of the show, the bouts the entire premium live event is sold around.

Who will be involved in those feud-ending wars of attrition, held in two rings and surrounded by unforgiving an unforgiving steel cage?

One answer is fairly obvious. The other? Maybe not as much.

The Bloodline: Roman Reigns, Jey Uso, Jimmy Uso, Solo Sikoa, and Jacob Fatu

The 946: Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price, Carmelo Hayes, and LA Knight

This is the easier of the two matches to predict.

A war between The Bloodline and 946 has been the obvious direction for War Games for the last two months and the players are almost complete, especially with the reveal of Hayes as the newest member of the 946 this past Monday on Raw.

The Bloodline suffered a brutal beatdown, with The Usos and Sikoa on the receiving end, but reinforcements should be coming soon. Reigns will be off the red carpet and finish his promotional duties for Street Fighter while Fatu should be back after being run over by Jaida Parker.

That begs the question: who does the 946 turn to in order to round out the team? It does not have to be someone who will join the group or stand alongside it every week. It can be someone with a common enemy in the Bloodline. That person should be LA Knight, who already teased that things may not be as cool between him and Sikoa as they were two months ago.

The Megastar has unfinished business with Reigns and aligning himself with The OTC's biggest rivals right now might be the best way for him to avenge his most crushing defeat yet.

The real question is whether Naomi returns to neutralize Parker and prevent her from getting involved, a moment that would spark excitement, further intrigue in the rivalry, and an unforgettable moment at a premium live event that does not typically have an abundance of them these days.

Team 1: Chelsea Green, Tiffany Stratton, Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, and Tatum Paxley

Team 2: Jacy Jayne, Fallon Henley, Lainey Reid, Nia Jax, and Lash Legend

The SmackDown women's division has been dominated by factions and tag teams in 2026 so what better way to spotlight the blue brand at Survivor Series than by booking it in the women's War Games match.

The babyface team feels somewhat obvious, WWE Women's Champion Green leading a team that also involved two-time Money in the Bank winner Stratton, Flair, and WWE Women's Tag Team Champions Paxley and Bliss.

On the heel side, the hated Fatal Influence's Jayne, Henley, and Reid. The only question is whether Jax and Legend make sense to round the team out or if it should be some mixture of Jade Cargill, Michin, and B-Fab.

Considering Stratton outlasted Legend to win the briefcase at Money in the Bank, there is a natural rivalry there that can build in the coming weeks and lead to the two-cage battle.

A less-heated showdown than the men's match, there are still plenty of story threads and intriguing interactions to make this one a worthy opener at the annual Fall spectacular.

articles.summary: Alex Ovechkin will retire after the 2026-27 season, closing a 22-year NHL career played entirely for the Washington Capitals.
articles.body: Alex Ovechkin will retire after the 2026-27 season, closing a 22-year NHL career played entirely for the Washington Capitals. The 41-year-old captain told his teammates before practice on Monday, October 5, in Arlington, Virginia. He leaves as the league's all-time leading goal scorer, with 929 goals at the time of the announcement and the 2018 Stanley Cup on his résumé. He signed a one-year contract on July 2 and shared the news before the home opener against Pittsburgh so he could concentrate on the games.How did Alex Ovechkin go from a young Russian star to a Capitals icon?Alex Ovechkin was 20 when he debuted on October 5, 2005, against the Columbus Blue Jackets. On his first shift, he hit defenseman Radoslav Suchy so hard that a pane of glass behind the net came loose. Then he scored twice in a 3-2 win. Washington still finished last in the Southeast Division that year at 29-41-12, but the building had changed. Ovechkin scored 52 goals and won the Calder Trophy as the league's top rookie.The wins came slower than the highlights. The Capitals made the playoffs for the first time with him in 2007-08, the year he took the Art Ross Trophy with 112 points. They won the Presidents' Trophy in 2009-10, 2015-16 and 2016-17, yet never got past the second round. He collected three Hart Trophies as league MVP and still heard the same question every spring.That changed in his 13th season. The Capitals beat Pittsburgh, Tampa Bay and Vegas on the way to the 2018 Stanley Cup, and Ovechkin led the NHL with 15 playoff goals and won the Conn Smythe Trophy. "Everybody knew he was going to be a legend of the game, but to be considered a legend of the game, you have to win the Stanley Cup," teammate Tom Wilson said.Why is Alex Ovechkin retiring after the 2026-27 season?He points to his family and his body. Ovechkin made the call this summer after talking with his wife, Nastya. "I'm not 20 years old and I want to play with my kids when they're growing up playing hockey, playing soccer, playing basketball. I want to be healthy enough to do that kind of stuff," he said.The news did not land out of nowhere. Wilson and Dylan Strome said Ovechkin hinted at it last week during a team dinner in Annapolis, Maryland. "You never know after a couple beers if it's like full-truth or half-truth or what," Wilson said. Coach Spencer Carbery only knew for certain when Ovechkin called him on Sunday.Washington spent the summer adding Alex Tuch, Jordan Kyrou, Boone Jenner and Vincent Desharnais after missing the playoffs last season. Ovechkin played all 82 games and led the team with 32 goals and 64 points, yet the Capitals finished three points behind Philadelphia for third in the Metropolitan Division.How did Alex Ovechkin change hockey in Washington?Former goalie Olie Kolzig played 16 seasons for the Capitals and now works in player development for the club. He has a short answer. "He totally turned D.C. into a 100 percent hockey town where maybe that wasn't the case," Kolzig said. Washington went back to red as its primary home jersey color in 2007-08, and the "Rock the Red" era followed, with crowds in red filling the arena.The numbers back him up. USA Hockey counted 12,856 registered players in Washington, Maryland and Virginia in 2005-06, Ovechkin's rookie year. Its most recent report, from 2024-25, lists 22,222. That is a 73 percent jump, and the area calls it the Ovechkin Effect. Wilson sees it in the kids who grew up watching him. "There's hundreds of thousands of kids that have played the game because of him and look up to him every day," he said.What made the Alex Ovechkin and Sidney Crosby rivalry so special?Neither player got a vote on being compared. The Capitals took Ovechkin first overall in 2004. Pittsburgh took Sidney Crosby first in 2005, after a lockout wiped out a full season. Ovechkin won the Calder with 106 points, and Crosby finished second with 102.The playoffs gave it teeth. They met four times, always in the second round. Pittsburgh won in 2009, 2016 and 2017 and lifted the Cup each time. Washington finally won in 2018 and did the same.Time softened it. "He's had a huge impact on it, on and off the ice," Crosby said last season. Evgeni Malkin rarely speaks after morning skates, but he made an exception on Monday and said Ovechkin "did everything for a team, a league."What records is Alex Ovechkin leaving behind?Start with goals. Ovechkin passed Wayne Gretzky's 894 on April 6, 2025, with his 895th at the New York Islanders, a mark long viewed as out of reach. Add 77 playoff goals and his total of 1,006 sits second in NHL history to Gretzky's 1,016.The shelf is crowded. He holds the records for power-play goals (331), game-winning goals (141), overtime goals (27) and empty-net goals (72). He has the most 30-goal seasons (20) and 40-goal seasons (14), and he ties Gretzky and Mike Bossy with nine 50-goal seasons.Durability may be the quieter record. Last year he became the fifth player to play all 82 games at age 40 or older. He has missed only 51 games to injury, and his 3,881 hits are third most since the league began counting them in 2005-06. Former linemate Chris Clark says fans miss what teammates saw. "I think he'd trade that all away for two or three more Stanley Cups," Clark said.What happens next for Ovechkin and the Capitals?Do not expect Ovechkin to chase a farewell tour. "I'm going to focus on my game," he said. "I'm going to focus to help the team to win. Obviously, if some different teams want to do something, yeah, why not? But to be honest with you, I'm not going to pay attention to that."Strome laid out the team's aim. "Our goal is to obviously compete for a Stanley Cup and give Ovi the best chance to have one more," he said.Where he plays next is still open. He has floated finishing with Moscow Dynamo, the program where he grew up, but he has made no announcement.Stay updated with the latest Asian Games 2026 news, check the Asian Games medal tally and complete Asian Games schedule.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Texas coach Sarkisian moves closer to adding to his trophy case
articles.summary: Steve Sarkisian moves closer to national honor. The Texas Longhorns head coach has been named to the watch list for the 2026 Dodd Trophy.
articles.body:
As the college football season hits its halfway point, Longhorns head coach Steve Sarkisian is moving closer to adding to his trophy case. On Tuesday, Sarkisian was named to the midseason watch list for the 2026 Dodd Trophy , the Bobby Dodd Coach of the Year. The award honors the head coach of a team who enjoys success on the gridiron, while also stressing the importance of scholarship, leadership, and integrity.

Tuesday's honor comes as no surprise given how the Longhorns have performed. They are off to a 4-1 start and currently ranked seventh in the country. Although they lost to Oklahoma last week in a disappointing fashion, Texas is still in the conversation for a national title.

For Sarkisian, this is not unfamiliar territory. This is the fourth time he has earned a spot on the award's midseason watch list while at Texas. With Sarkisian leading the way, the Longhorns have been in the AP Top 10 for seven consecutive weeks this season. They also have two wins over ranked teams, which is tied for the most in the nation.

Additionally, the Longhorns have etched themselves into the record books this year. In their first three games, Sarkisian's team recorded at least 25 first downs. Texas did that only once before, in 2008. Regardless of the opponent, the Longhorns have been hard to beat.

This weekend, they will put a disappointing loss in the rearview mirror as they take on Florida. If the Longhorns avoid mistakes and penalties, they should emerge victorious.

Although the season is far from over, Sarkisian has a good chance to add another honor to his already impressive resume.
