articles.title: Overreacting to Dylan Larkin, the Flyers, the Rangers and the Start of the 2026-27 NHL Season
articles.summary: We're less than one month into the 2026-27 NHL season, and absolute chaos has already ensued.
articles.body:
We're less than one month into the 2026-27 NHL season, and absolute chaos has already ensued.

We've seen an Igor Shesterkin goalie goal followed by the devastating injury that took him out for the season . We've struggled through a terrible Flames team and a somehow arguably worse Flyers team. We've got the reigning Champion Hurricanes picking up right where they left off as they lead the league with a six-game winning streak and the league's best record (6-1-1).

We haven't seen it all yet, but we've seen enough to start forming the opinions that will become the hills we gladly die on all season. Here are five overreactions to the start of the 2026-27 NHL season.

The Flames Are Going to Be Historically Bad

Hey, we've gotta hand it to the Flames: They got their first win of the season during Tuesday's Frozen Frenzy in a 4-2 win over the Ducks. You gotta start somewhere, and 1-5-0 is at least better than the Flyers' winless start to the season — we'll get to Philly.

The lone win doesn't take away from just how brutal Calgary's start to the season has been, though. The four goals in Tuesday's game took them up to averaging just two goals per game, and that's despite taking plenty of shots. Their -17 goal differential is second-worst in the NHL. Worst of all, typically solid Dustin Wolf is sporting a 4.56 goals-against average and an .839 save percentage.

Fear not, Calgary fans; this is all part of the process, and this is exactly where we expected the Flames to be at this stage of the rebuild. Still, they objectively stink, and they could have one of the worst NHL seasons ever if they keep it up.

The Canes Are Definitely Going Back-to-Back

The reigning Stanley Cup Champions have picked up exactly where they left off this season, leading the league with 13 standings points, a 6-1-1 record, and a six-game winning streak.

Sebastian Aho is off to his best career start, ranked third league-wide in points with six goals and 13 points in eight games. No Freddie Andersen, no problem so far: Pyotr Kochetkov is crushing it in net with a 4-0 record, a .911 save percentage, and a 1.73 goals-against average.

The team as a whole ranks No. 4 in the league in goals per game with 3.88, and fifth with 2.38 goals against per game. The Canes are back to being a jack of all trades, and yes, a master of all trades as well.

The Flyers' Problems Are More Than Just a Coach and Lack of a No. 1 Center

As terrible as the start to the Flames' season has been, it was completely expected and even embraced as part of their rebuild.

The Flyers, on the other hand, made it two rounds into last season's playoffs with their promising young core. They had their concerns headed into the season, like that glaring hole in the all-important first-line center role and goalie Dan Vladar's training camp injury. Plus, they likely overachieved last season, and most of us came into this one wondering if they'd be able to maintain a playoff spot, let alone take a step forward, without addressing the aforementioned issues and then some.

The Flyers have kicked off the NHL season on an eight-game losing streak and a 0-5-3 record. They're the only team in the league yet to win, and they own the league's worst goal differential at -21.

Defense hasn't been their strong suit in this era, and it's even worse than last season. Meanwhile, scoring has been virtually non-existent: Trevor Zegras and Porter Martone have just one goal apiece in eight games. The young core is going to have to turn things around on the scoresheet to, uh, win at least one game, let alone make the playoffs.

The Rangers Will Still Make The Playoffs Without Shesterkin

The news that Igor Shesterkin was out for the season was going to be devastating no matter what, but it stung even more because the Rangers were off to an incredible start.

They came into the season immediately correcting last season's scoring woes, including a goal from Shesterkin himself. The new additions, such as Sean Durzi and Marcus Pettersson, were fitting in swimmingly; the "kids" looked fantastic, and the team overall looked slated for a bounce-back year.

The good news? None of that has stopped in Shesterkin's absence. The Rangers are second only to the Hurricanes in the Metro with a 6-2-0 record, 12 points, and a goal differential of 13. Dylan Garand has been admirable stepping in for Shesterkin, sporting a 3-1-0 record with a 1.15 goals-against average and a .951 save percentage. New York is second in the league with just 1.75 goals against per game in total, and on the offensive side, the Blueshirts are averaging a respectable 3.38.

Not only will New York be just fine, but they're also going to make it back to the playoffs. In the biggest plot twist of all, it will have to be without Shesterkin.

The Red Wings Should Embrace the Tank and Trade Dylan Larkin and Simon Edvinsson Now

The Flyers and the Flames might own the worst records in the league to start the season, but the Red Wings definitely own the worst vibes.

They're at the bottom of the Atlantic with a 1-3-2 record, four points, and a negative six-goal differential. They're averaging less than three goals per game, and while they're scoring a decent 3.17 goals per game, it doesn't appear to be sustainable whatsoever.

This team has an extremely shaky foundation right now: no permanent GM , with Shawn Horcoff serving as the interim, and a checked-out former captain in Dylan Larkin, who remains in limbo. Why not just embrace a tank at this point and trade Larkin and Simon Edvinsson, who has also reportedly requested a trade ? I guess that would require a permanent GM, huh?

The Wings reportedly locked up Alex DeBrincat to a $91 million contract Tuesday , but that's a drop in the bucket for the work that needs to be done to fix this team.

articles.title: Opponent Breakdown: Syracuse Orange Offense
articles.summary: Fran Brown led the Syracuse football program to 10 wins in his first season, and he’s been trying to get back to that standard ever since. Brown has had a st...
articles.body:
Fran Brown led the Syracuse football program to 10 wins in his first season, and he's been trying to get back to that standard ever since. Brown has had a string of tough injuries that have hindered his ability to get things back on track, but his teams compete well, and he has done a good job of bringing in good talent to a place that is not easy to recruit.

It will be up in the air for which quarterback the Cards face this weekend as the Orange have been killed by injuries again at the position. Steve Angeli was the opening day starter, but he has been ineffective on top of being hurt. Malachi Nelson was forced into action last weekend as the third-stringer. Amari Odom was who I initially thought would start, but it sounds like Angeli is back to practicing this week.

Angeli was a revelation last season for the Orange as he started the season with 10 touchdown passes and 329 yards per game before he was lost for the season in their fifth game. He returned as the starter this year, but he has not been the same player. Angeli has completed 49% of his passes with one touchdown and five picks against FBS competition. He was benched in favor of Odom, and I would argue that Malachi Nelson looked better in his limited time. But Fran Brown expects Angeli to play if he can practice this entire week.

Odom is an athletic pocket passer who starred at Kennesaw State last season. He got the start against UConn, finishing the game by completing 73% of his passes for over 300 yards. Odom is not a running quarterback, but he can beat you with his legs, and he can avoid sacks and pick up a first down on a scramble. I would not expect Syracuse to call designed runs for him. While Odom has looked poised in the limited time he's had, I don't know that he's been in a situation against a defense with the athletes Louisville has.

If Angeli or Odom can't go against Louisville, the Orange may have to start their fourth-string quarterback, Danny Lauter. The transfer from Georgetown was forced into the game last week against Virginia when Nelson was injured. He went 2-for-6 with a nice throw for a touchdown, though the pass probably should have been intercepted.

This offense wants to throw the ball around, but they do a good job of getting their running backs going in the running game as well. Tylik Hill and his 101 rushing yards per game lead this group of backs who share the workload. Hill is a back with solid speed, but his vision and ability to find seams on interior runs is very good. He has broken a handful of explosive runs this year, where he has shown patience to find a path through the defense to get himself into open space.

Ahmad Miller and Shavane Anderson are very capable backups. Miller is the short-yardage back, but he has also had a few chunk plays in the open field this year. Anderson is a true freshman who comes in as one of the best players in the history of New Jersey football. He is a solid balance of the other two backs, but it stands out to me that he runs very hard for a freshman. These three players have been good for the Orange, and the Cards will have to continue to play the run well this weekend.

The Orange have a handful of solid receivers, led by Umari Hatcher on the outside. The 6-3/190 veteran has been outstanding this season, as he leads the ACC in touchdowns. Hatcher is also ranked in the top five in just about every other receiver statistic. He is consistently putting up big games for the Orange, and it's obvious that the offense is featuring him as each quarterback makes him the main target.

Justus Ross-Simmons is the second-leading receiver on the team, and he is another big receiver on the outside. The Orange don't have a lot of speed at receiver, but Ross-Simmons is a solid deep threat. Daunte Bacheiye has also been a reliable deep threat for the team. He is listed as a tight end, but he's played on the outside a lot this year. Five-star freshman Calvil Russell could also see his role expand as he comes back from an injury.

For the second straight week, the Cards' edge rushers will have the chance to go up against an offensive tackle who has struggled this season. Kam Pringle is among the national leaders in pressures allowed, per PFF. The Cards were able to pressure the quarterback 8 times last weekend against Xavier Chaplan, who is the left tackle for FSU. As this defense adjusts to the more aggressive plan that we saw last weekend, we should see them taking advantage of these matchups. The Cuse line has given up too many pressures as a group, but Pringle's performance has been particularly egregious.

articles.title: Jim Nantz offers first comments on Tony Romo departure: ‘I think unquestionably he will work again’
articles.summary: It’s been 12 days since CBS Sports formally split from NFL analyst Tony Romo after his OWI arrest in Wisconsin over the summer. During that time, his former...
articles.body:
It's been 12 days since CBS Sports formally split from NFL analyst Tony Romo after his OWI arrest in Wisconsin over the summer. During that time, his former partner of nine years, Jim Nantz, has kept mum on the topic. Nantz remains the top play-by-play voice at CBS and has been calling games alongside J.J. Watt this season while the network, which had suspended Romo following his arrest, determined his old partner's fate.

Now that the dust has seemingly settled, and the Nantz-Watt duo will continue together for the rest of the season, Nantz is offering his first public comments on Romo's departure. In a recent episode of the Traina Thoughts podcast, Nantz addressed CBS' decision to let go of Romo, and suggested that the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback will be back working in media at some point down the line.

"I think unquestionably he will work again," Nantz told host Jimmy Traina. "I don't know if it's calling games or being in studio, but he's got a lot of talent. He's got a lot of people who like him, and he's a star. He's got a personality that's different, and that's a good thing. …And I don't know where Tony's head is on that right now, so I'm not going to speculate, but I think you're asking me 'will he ever work again in the business?' I think there will be plenty of opportunity for that, because he's got game."

Nantz was very complimentary of Romo throughout the interview, echoing much of the same sentiment he shared with Awful Announcing at CBS' NFL preview event over the summer.

"It's a forever relationship [with Romo]," Nantz explained when asked about where he stands with his old partner. "It was a great friendship before we got started as teammates on the air, I've talked about it through the years that when he was a player, with his love of golf … when I would have a Cowboys game we would spend a lot of time, devote a lot of time in these production meetings to talking about golf. So it was a friendship that went back, I'd say [to] 2010."

He also stressed that the decision to bench, and subsequently separate from Romo, was made entirely by CBS Sports and division president David Berson.

"I had no role in this … and I think that's the way it had to be. It was going to be CBS Sports' decision and Dave Berson," Nantz said. "I had no role. No role in that whatsoever."

As for his new partner J.J. Watt, Nantz was similarly complimentary, specifically praising Watt's preparation. Nantz, however, stressed multiple times that his assessment of Watt was not a direct comparison to Romo.

"Let me just say, if this gets clipped and posted, I want this to be included that I'm not making any comparisons. So anything I say about J.J. is not a reflection of what I wasn't seeing with Tony," Nantz prefaced. "…[Watt's] preparation is so much like a guy that is preparing for an actual game, to play in it. It's astounding to see the level of detail he gets into, and that he shares. I find that to be so commendable that, here we are midweek, I expect an email coming in any day now that will already begun the process for him of breaking down almost every player that's going to be on the field this coming Sunday, and seeing things that have popped off the screen for him. He's just a total pro of making sure that we as a group … we all are aware of what he sees going on."

Now, it's understandable why Nantz would preempt such praise of Watt with the caveat that he is not making a direct comparison with Romo, as one of the most common criticisms of Romo's recent years in the booth was that he sounded unprepared. It's only fair to take Nantz at his word, that he's not comparing the two announcers, but it is certainly interesting that his top plaudit for Watt was one of Romo's apparent shortcomings.

Nantz and Watt will continue their partnership in Week 6 for the Bills-Raiders game in Las Vegas.
